issues.title: Scaffold repository tooling
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor, I want the repository rules, hooks and CI in place so that every change runs through an issue, a branch, the full test gate and a pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/settings.json`, `hooks/issue-context.sh`, `hooks/branch-guard.sh` and its test suite are in place and pass
- [ ] `.claude/skills/gh/SKILL.md` describes the issue, branch and PR workflow for this repo
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` covers containers only (Makefile, Go 1.26), issue branches, four test layers, `make openapi`, no mocks below the layer under test, and style rules
- [ ] `run-tests.sh` is the single gate: shell tests, Go format/vet/unit, OpenAPI drift, web lint/types/vitest, compose-backed integration and Playwright on ports derived per worktree
- [ ] `release.sh` and its tests are ported; `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `./run-tests.sh`; issue templates and a PR template with `Closes #` exist
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` record the architecture and the decisions taken so far
- [ ] `NOTICE` credits the Apache-2.0 code adapted from Armature

## Tests

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh` and `tests/test-release.sh` run inside `run-tests.sh` and in CI.

issues.title: Backend skeleton: config, database, migrations, HTTP route table
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Go service skeleton that mirrors Armature so that every later feature plugs into the same patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `backend/cmd/{api,worker,migrate,seed,openapi}` build
- [ ] Configuration from `STATOR_*` environment variables only, with validation and sentence-style errors
- [ ] `internal/db` cluster with primary/replica transactions and org row-level security via `current_org_id()`; IDs from `uuidv7()`
- [ ] goose migrations embedded and applied by `cmd/migrate`; `org` and `app_user` tables exist with RLS policies
- [ ] chi router with middleware chain (request id, metrics, logging, recovery, security headers, same-site check, timeout, authenticate) and a single error envelope
- [ ] The route table generates `api/openapi.json`; a unit test fails when the committed spec is stale and when router and table disagree
- [ ] `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` respond

## Tests

Unit tests for config and route table; integration test proving RLS isolates two orgs even through raw SQL.

issues.title: Web skeleton: routing, API client, app shell
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want a fast single-page app with a clear shell (rail, sidebar, content) so that navigating the wiki feels like Armature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Router and Query
- [ ] openapi-fetch client typed from `web/src/api/schema.d.ts` generated from `api/openapi.json`
- [ ] Shell with rail, collapsible sidebar, top bar with search entry point and user menu
- [ ] Error and empty states follow Armature's design docs; user-facing constants live in `web/src/config.ts`
- [ ] ESLint, `tsc --noEmit` and vitest wired into `run-tests.sh`

## Tests

Vitest for shell components; Playwright smoke test loads the app and navigates.

issues.title: Compose stack and Makefile with containerised toolchains
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want `make up` to start the complete stack and every toolchain to run in a container so that nothing has to be installed on the host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deploy/docker-compose.yml` with postgres, valkey, seaweedfs, mailpit, keycloak (realm with clients for Stator and Armature), migrate, seed, api, worker, web and armature-stub
- [ ] Dockerfiles for backend and web; nginx config for the web image
- [ ] Makefile targets: up, down, clean, logs, seed, test, test-integration, test-e2e (ONLY=, WORKERS=), test-all, openapi, vet, fmt, npm ARGS=, web-build, shell
- [ ] Go 1.26 and Node run as containers with caches under `.cache/`
- [ ] Compose project name and host ports derive from the worktree path so parallel worktrees do not collide

## Tests

`run-tests.sh` brings the stack up and down; CI proves it on a clean runner.

issues.title: Single sign-on via OIDC with sessions and group sync
issues.body:
## User story

As an organisation admin, I want members to log in through our identity provider and have their groups follow them so that access is managed in one place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One OIDC provider per organisation (issuer, client id, secret, scopes, groups claim, enabled), configurable by admins
- [ ] Login via `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start` and `/auth/oidc/callback`; users are created or updated by subject
- [ ] Groups from the groups claim are synced into Stator groups
- [ ] Sessions in an HttpOnly cookie; only the SHA-256 of the token is stored; logout and expiry work
- [ ] Backchannel issuer rewrite for in-cluster access, as in Armature
- [ ] Optional local password login for bootstrap admins (argon2)

## Tests

Unit tests for claim mapping; integration tests against Keycloak in compose; Playwright login fixture used by all e2e tests.

issues.title: Themes: design tokens, light/dark, custom themes, import
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want Stator to look and feel exactly like Armature, including my custom themes, so that both tools read as one product.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens identical to Armature's Clay light and dark values
- [ ] Light / dark / system switch stored per browser and applied before first paint
- [ ] Server-stored custom themes with the same spec as Armature (colors, fonts, shape, shadows, cursors, icons, backdrop, effect, css) and the same limits
- [ ] Built-in Deep-Tech and Constellation themes; organisation default theme
- [ ] Import and export in the `armature-theme/1` format, so Armature theme files work unchanged
- [ ] Theme editor with live preview

## Tests

Vitest: token list matches the stylesheet, compiler output; integration: theme CRUD and import; Playwright: switch themes and import `minecraft.armature-theme.json`.

issues.title: Playwright end-to-end harness
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Playwright suite running against the real compose stack so that every user flow is proven in a browser before it is pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `e2e/` Playwright project with TypeScript, base URL from the per-worktree ports
- [ ] Fixtures: logged-in user via Keycloak, fresh organisation per test file, seeded data helpers through the API
- [ ] Traces and screenshots on failure, uploaded as CI artifacts
- [ ] Runs from `run-tests.sh` and `make test-e2e` with `ONLY=` and `WORKERS=`

## Tests

The harness proves itself with a login smoke test.

issues.title: Responsive layout and accessibility baseline
issues.body:
## User story

As a user on a phone or with assistive technology, I want every screen to be usable so that nobody is locked out of the documentation.

issues.title: Spaces with home page and space settings
issues.body:

issues.title: Page tree with drag-and-drop, move and copy
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to arrange pages in a nested tree so that readers find related content together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pages have a parent and a rank; unlimited nesting
- [ ] Sidebar tree with lazy loading, expand/collapse and keyboard support

- [ ] Move and copy a page with or without its children, also into another space

Unit: rank maths; integration: move/copy including subtree and permission checks; Playwright: drag a page under another.

issues.title: Trash and restore
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want deleted pages to go to a trash so that mistakes can be undone.

- [ ] Deleting a page moves it and its children to the space trash

Integration: delete/restore/purge; Playwright: delete and restore a page.

issues.title: Rich-text editor: formatting, slash menu, tables, code, panels, anchors
issues.body:

- [ ] Headings, bold, italic, strike, code, links, lists, task-style checklists, quotes, horizontal rule
- [ ] Markdown-style shortcuts as you type and on paste
- [ ] Slash menu listing every insertable block, filterable by typing

- [ ] Panels: info, note, success, warning, error

## Tests

Unit (Go): document validation; vitest: extensions; Playwright: slash menu, table, code block, panel, heading link.

issues.title: Full-text search with filters and quick search
issues.body:
## User story

issues.title: Permissions: global, space and page restrictions
issues.body:
## User story

As an admin, I want to control who can see and edit which content so that sensitive documentation stays protected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Global permissions: use Stator, create spaces, administer
- [ ] Space permissions per user and group: view, add pages, add comments, delete, administer
- [ ] Page restrictions for view and edit, inherited by child pages
- [ ] Enforced in the service and in the database; attempts through raw SQL are refused as well
- [ ] UI shows why a page is restricted and who can access it

## Tests

Integration: permission matrix including a raw-SQL attempt; Playwright: restricted page is hidden from another user.

issues.title: Attachments
issues.body:

As an author, I want to attach files and images by dragging or pasting so that pages can carry screenshots and documents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upload via drag-and-drop, paste and file picker; stored in S3-compatible storage

issues.title: REST API with OpenAPI and personal access tokens
issues.body:
## User story

As an integrator, I want a documented API and personal tokens so that scripts and other tools can read and write content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All UI operations are available under `/api/v1` and described in `api/openapi.json`, served at `/api/v1/openapi.json`
- [ ] Personal access tokens with prefix, optional expiry and optional read-only scope; only hashes stored
- [ ] Token management UI

## Tests

Integration: every response is validated against the spec and the suite fails if an operation is not exercised; Playwright: create and revoke a token.

issues.title: Page comments

issues.title: Inline comments
issues.body:
## User story

As a reviewer, I want to comment on a specific passage so that feedback is precise.

## Acceptance criteria

Vitest: anchor mark; integration: resolve flow; Playwright: comment on a selection and resolve.

issues.title: Mentions

Unit: mention extraction; integration: notification and access check; Playwright: mention a user.

issues.title: Watch pages and spaces
issues.body:

issues.title: In-app and email notifications
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want to be notified in the app and by email so that I never miss a mention or an important change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Notification centre with unread badge, mark read, mark all read

issues.title: Connect an Armature instance
issues.body:
## User story

As an admin and as a user, I want to connect Stator to Armature so that pages can show and create issues with my own rights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Org admins set the Armature base URL
- [ ] Each user stores their Armature personal access token under Profile; encrypted at rest with `STATOR_SECRET_KEY`
- [ ] Every Armature call is made as the viewing user through the SSRF guard; no shared bot token for reads
- [ ] Clear message and connect button when a user has not connected yet
- [ ] `cmd/armature-stub` implements the Armature API subset used; a contract test checks it against Armature's `api/openapi.json`

## Tests

Unit: token encryption; integration: proxy against the stub; Playwright: connect flow.

issues.title: Smart links for Armature issues
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want Armature issue keys and URLs to turn into live chips so that readers see status at a glance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pasting an Armature issue URL or typing a known issue key converts it to a chip
- [ ] Chip shows key, summary, type icon and status, with a hover card
- [ ] Readers without access see only the key

## Tests

Vitest: key detection; Playwright: paste a URL against the stub.

issues.title: Armature issue block
issues.body:

- [ ] Shows summary, status, assignee, priority; refreshes on view

Integration: proxy and cache; Playwright: insert and render the block.

issues.title: Armature issue list block from a query

Integration: search proxy; Playwright: insert a list and see rows.

issues.title: Create Armature issues from selected text
issues.body:

As an author, I want to turn selected text into Armature issues so that action items from a document become tracked work.

issues.title: Show pages that mention an issue in Armature
issues.body:

As an Armature user, I want to see which documentation pages reference an issue so that I can jump to the spec.

Integration: sync against the stub; manual check against a local Armature.

issues.title: Receive Armature webhooks to refresh cached issues
issues.body:
## User story

As a reader, I want issue chips and blocks to reflect changes promptly so that pages never show stale status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/api/v1/armature/webhook` verifies `X-Armature-Signature-256` with a per-org secret
- [ ] issue.updated, issue.transitioned and comment.added invalidate the cached entries
- [ ] Setup instructions shown in the admin integration screen

## Tests

Unit: signature check; integration: invalidation.

issues.title: Use my active Armature theme

issues.title: Backup and restore
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want documented backup and restore so that no data is lost.

## Decision

The first version is an operator backup, not an in-app export: one command takes a consistent database dump plus a copy of every object in storage, and one command restores it. Two install paths are covered, Docker Compose and the Helm chart. Scheduled backups with retention are out of scope for now; a site-wide export from the UI would be a separate issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Docker Compose**: a backup command writes one archive (database dump, object storage contents, the Stator version it was taken with); a restore command brings an empty stack back from it and refuses an archive from a newer version.
- [ ] **Helm chart**: CloudNativePG backups to object storage and the attachment bucket configured through chart values, with a documented restore into a fresh release.
- [ ] `docs/backup-and-restore.md` covers both paths, what is and is not in a backup (for example secrets and Keycloak), and how to check a restore.
- [ ] **Restore tested in CI**: fill a stack with pages, versions, attachments, comments and permissions, back it up, wipe it, restore it, and check everything is back and readable through the API, including the row level security on restored rows.

## Tests

Unit tests for the archive and its refusals, a chart test for the jobs, an integration test that every PL/pgSQL function pins its search_path (a dump restores with an empty one), and the backup round trip as a layer of its own against the compose stack.

issues.title: Read your own writes when a replica serves reads
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want to see my own change right after I make it, so that a save never seems to be lost because the next read hit a replica that hasn't caught up yet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Writes return their LSN (the db cluster already does this). After a write, the API pins that session's reads to the primary until the replica has replayed that position, as Armature does with its Valkey-backed tracker (`ARMATURE_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`).
- [ ] Tracked per session in Valkey, with a TTL from `STATOR_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`.
- [ ] Handlers stop discarding the write position.
- [ ] The integration suite runs with the replica configured again (`mk/stack.mk` currently leaves it out of the suite's environment for this reason).

## Tests

Integration: write then immediately read through the API with the replica configured, repeated enough times to catch lag. The theme tests that failed with the replica pass.

issues.title: Kubernetes deployment with CloudNativePG read and write services
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator running Stator on Kubernetes, I want a CloudNativePG cluster whose write service takes all writes and whose read service takes the reads, so that read traffic scales across replicas and the primary stays free for writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Helm chart `deploy/charts/stator`, modelled on Armature's `deploy/charts/armature`:
  - `cnpg.enabled` renders a `postgresql.cnpg.io/v1` Cluster (instances, storage, resources and backup passed through from `cnpg.spec`), as in Armature's `cnpg-cluster.yaml`
  - the api, worker, migrate and seed deployments and jobs, plus a roles job for `stator_app` / `stator_admin`
  - an ingress, a ServiceMonitor, and Valkey / S3 settings
- [ ] Write path: `STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_URL` points at `<cluster>-rw`. Migrations and admin work use it too.
- [ ] Read path: `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_URLS` points at `<cluster>-ro` when `cnpg.readReplicas` is on and `instances > 1`, otherwise it is empty and reads go to `-rw`. Same rules as Armature's `_helpers.tpl`.
- [ ] Reads stay correct behind a load-balanced `-ro` service, because one connection can land on any replica:
  - replica lag is sampled per connection and bounded (`STATOR_DB_MAX_REPLICA_LAG`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_LAG_SAMPLES`, as in Armature); a lagging replica falls back to the primary
  - read-your-writes (#120) checks `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()` on the connection it actually got, not on the service
- [ ] Separate pool sizes for the write and read pools (`STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_MAX_CONNS`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_MAX_CONNS`), plus Prometheus metrics per pool (queries, wait time, fallbacks to primary).
- [ ] Guard: `cnpg.enabled` and a bundled Postgres can't both be on; the chart fails with a sentence saying which to turn off.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and a deployment section in the README describe the write and read services.

## Tests

- Go unit tests for read routing: replica chosen, lag fallback, LSN pinning per connection.
- Integration against the compose primary and replica: pause replay on the replica (`pg_wal_replay_pause()`) and show that reads fall back to the primary and still see the last write.
- `helm lint` and `helm template` with cnpg on and off, with `instances: 1` and `instances: 3`, checked by a shell test in `run-tests.sh` (Helm runs in a container).

issues.title: Map identity provider groups to org roles
issues.body:
## User story

As an org admin, I want groups from our identity provider to grant roles in Stator, so that access follows what we already manage centrally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the SSO settings page, admins map IdP group names (values of the groups claim) to org roles (member, admin). Several groups can map to the same role.
- [ ] On every SSO sign-in, the person's role follows the mapping; the highest mapped role wins. When a group disappears, the role it granted goes too, but never below member while they are still a member.
- [ ] A mapped group counts as the admin's approval given in advance: a first sign-in by someone in a mapped group joins directly with that role. Everyone else still waits for approval (#5).
- [ ] Roles an admin set by hand for people outside any mapped group are left alone. The UI shows which roles come from the IdP.
- [ ] The org owner is never demoted by a mapping.
- [ ] Every role change the mapping makes is recorded for the audit log.

## Tests

- Unit tests for resolving the mapping.
- Integration through Keycloak: alice (`stator-administrators`) becomes admin once that group is mapped, and loses it when the group is removed in Keycloak.
- A Playwright case for the mapping UI.

issues.title: Give the not-found page a heading and let axe check headings in every test
issues.body:
The not-found page has no `h1`, so axe's `page-has-heading-one` rule fails on it. The shell tests don't catch this: without the caret measurement stubs from `web/src/test/layout.ts`, axe silently skips the rule in jsdom.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The not-found page (and every route) renders exactly one `h1`.
- [ ] The layout stubs load for all vitest tests (`web/src/test/setup.ts`), so axe checks `page-has-heading-one` everywhere.

## Tests

The existing axe tests pass with the stubs loaded globally.

issues.title: Throwaway organisations for end-to-end test isolation
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want every end-to-end spec file to run in its own throwaway organisation, so that specs run in parallel without sharing the `demo` org's data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test-only endpoint, enabled only when `STATOR_TEST_ENDPOINTS=1` (set in compose for the suite, never by the Helm chart), creates an org with a unique slug. Alice (admin) and bob (member) are pre-approved in it, and its SSO provider points at the compose Keycloak realm.
- [ ] A matching endpoint deletes that org and all its data, including S3 objects.
- [ ] Sign-in works for any such slug.
- [ ] `e2e/fixtures/org.ts` `freshOrg` uses these endpoints. The theme specs move from the shared `demo` org to their own org and run in parallel again.
- [ ] The endpoints return 404 when the setting is off. An integration test proves it.

## Tests

- Integration: create, use and delete an org, and the 404 when disabled.
- The theme specs run in parallel.

issues.title: Make scrollable editor regions reachable from the keyboard
issues.body:
axe reports `scrollable-region-focusable` for the slash menu's scrolling list and for the `[data-dev-json]` box on `/dev/editor`. Keyboard users can't scroll content they can't focus.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scrollable regions can be scrolled from the keyboard. Make them focusable with a label, or keep the active option in view so the list itself never needs focus (the slash menu uses `aria-activedescendant`).
- [ ] Remove the matching entries from the known findings in `e2e/fixtures/shell.ts`.

The Playwright axe checks on `/dev/editor` pass with no known findings for this rule.

- [ ] A vitest test computes the contrast of every text token against every surface token from `index.css`, in both modes, and fails below 4.5:1 (3:1 for tokens used only for large text or icons, listed explicitly).
- [ ] Remove the `color-contrast` entry from the known findings in `e2e/fixtures/shell.ts`.
- [ ] The same values are proposed to Armature (see the linked Armature issue), so both products stay identical.

## Tests

- Vitest contrast matrix.
- Playwright axe with colour contrast in light and dark.

issues.title: Give code highlighting colours AA contrast on code blocks
issues.body:
In light mode the syntax colour for strings in code blocks (chart-2 / success, #2e7d4f) reaches only 4.13:1 on `surface-sunken`, the code block background. The Playwright suite never ran axe on a highlighted document, so it wasn't caught. Found while fixing #133.

issues.title: Let touch scroll the slash and mention lists again
issues.body:
#132 made the slash menu and the mention list `overflow-y-hidden`, scrolling them only by the active option, the arrow keys and the mouse wheel (handled by hand). On touch screens a swipe no longer scrolls these lists. People can still filter by typing and tap what they see, but on a phone the lower options of the 16-block slash menu are hard to reach.

issues.title: Root out flaky tests in the vitest and Playwright suites
issues.body:
Tests that failed once and then passed:

1. **ThemeEditor vitest:** timed out once at 5 s during a full gate. It passes on its own.
2. **`login.spec.ts` "a Keycloak user nobody has approved waits…":** a Keycloak redirect timeout once.
3. **Shared `demo` org:** specs that apply a theme leak it into specs running in parallel in `demo`. With colour contrast enforced (#133), an imported theme with poor contrast fails unrelated axe checks, for example `keyboard.spec.ts` on mobile. #131 moves theme specs into their own orgs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each flake has a root cause, fixed rather than retried. The ThemeEditor test waits on a condition instead of wall time; the Keycloak redirect gets an explicit wait on the right URL.
- [ ] Playwright runs with `retries: 0` locally and in CI, so flakes surface instead of hiding. If CI needs `retries: 1`, report retried tests as failures in a summary.
- [ ] Run the full suite 5 times in a row in CI (`workflow_dispatch` with a repeat input), all green.

issues.title: API contract for drafts, history, search, permissions and attachments

issues.title: Root out the flaky group roles sign-in integration test
issues.body:
`TestAMappedGroupGrantsItsRoleAndTakesItBack` (backend/test/group_roles_test.go) failed once in a pre-push gate on feat/20-attachments-api, which does not touch sign-in or roles; the full gate had just passed on the same commit, and a retry passed.

The test signs alice in through Keycloak several times in a row and reads her role after each sign-in. Under load, the sign-in path has been measured at up to about 5 s per step (see #137, fixed on the browser side in #148), so the integration client's timeouts, or a read that lands on the replica before the role change is visible there, are the first suspects.

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is found and fixed at its source, not by retrying or raising a timeout without a reason.
- The test passes 50 times in a row under the load of a parallel gate (`go test -run TestAMappedGroupGrantsItsRoleAndTakesItBack -count=50`).

## Tests

- Integration: the test above, repeated.

issues.title: Point a copied page's first version at the copy's own attachments
issues.body:
Copying a page copies its attachments and rewrites the copy's `image` and `attachment` nodes to the new ids (#150, through `page.Copy`'s copy hook). Versions (#149) give a copy a history row for version 1.

If that `page_version` row is written in the copy statement, before the hook rewrites `page.body`, the copy's version 1 still points at the original page's files. Viewing or restoring version 1 of the copy then shows files of another page, and they vanish when the original is purged.

## Acceptance criteria

- A copied page's version 1 in `page_version` references the copy's own attachments.
- Restoring version 1 of a copy shows the copy's files.
- Purging the original leaves every version of the copy intact.

## Tests

- Integration: copy a page with an image and a file, then read version 1 of the copy and compare its attachment ids with the copy's list; purge the original and read it again.

issues.title: Root out the flaky stored document keyboard scroll e2e test
issues.body:
The Playwright test "the editor › the stored document scrolls from the keyboard" (added in #141) failed once in a gate on feat/18-search-api, which does not touch the editor: after pressing PageDown in the stored-document region on `/dev/editor`, `scrollTop` stayed 0. The push gate right after passed.

Likely suspects: the region is not focused yet when the key is sent, or its content has not grown past its height when the test reads `scrollTop` (the stored document is written after the editor settles), so the key press has nothing to scroll.

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is found and fixed at its source, without retries or raised timeouts beyond a stated reason.
- The test passes with `REPEAT=100` under the load of a parallel gate.

## Tests

- e2e: the test above, repeated.

issues.title: Root out the flaky member removal notice in the join e2e spec
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/join.spec.ts:90` failed once under load (seen while proving #151): the "Carol Candidate was removed." notice did not appear within 5 s, although the removal had gone through (the cleanup's `DELETE` then got 404), and the cleanup's `GET /users` still listed carol.

#151 showed that read-your-writes is keyed per session on purpose, so a read under another session may land on a replica that has not replayed somebody else's write yet. Find out which session each step of this spec reads under:

- If the administrator's own page reads its own removal from a stale replica, that is a product bug in read-your-writes (the write is not noted, or the read is not pinned) and must be fixed in the product.
- If only the cleanup client reads under another key, the spec must wait for the replica (as `h.settle` does in the Go suite) or read under the page's own session.

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is named, and fixed in the product if the administrator's own read is stale.
- The spec passes with `REPEAT=100` under the load of a parallel gate.

## Tests

- e2e: the spec above, repeated; an integration test if the product changes.

issues.title: Make the versions e2e specs hold under load
issues.body:
The versions browser specs from #153 (`e2e/tests/versions.spec.ts`) failed several times in pre-push gates on feat/18-search-api while the host was heavily loaded (load average about 48 on 12 cores, five compose stacks). The branch does not touch the web side. The failures were timing: a draft stayed on "saving", and a new page was not yet visible where the spec expected it (a replica read). Run alone against a quiet stack the specs pass 15/15.

Two questions:

- Does the editor ever stay on "saving" for good when a draft save is slow or fails? That would be a product bug (a lost state transition), not only a slow test.
- Does any step read another person's write, or its own write under another session, without waiting for the replica, as #151 and #157 found elsewhere?

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause of each failure is named. A stuck "saving" state is fixed in the product if it can happen.
- The spec passes with `REPEAT=50` while a second full `make test-e2e` runs alongside.

## Tests

- e2e: the spec, repeated under load; vitest for any editor state fix.

issues.title: Root out the flaky autosave in the page blocks vitest
issues.body:
`web/src/features/editor/pageBlocks.test.tsx` (from #168) fails on some vitest runs, about 2 of 5 on a quiet machine: an autosave scheduled by `PageEditor.tsx` fires after the test environment has been torn down.

The fix belongs at the cause. Either the test waits for or flushes the pending save (fake timers, or unmounting the editor and awaiting its cleanup), or `PageEditor` cancels or awaits its pending save on unmount if that is a product bug too (a save firing after unmount would also hit real users who navigate away).

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is named; a save after unmount is fixed in the product if it can happen there.
- The file passes 50 runs in a row (`vitest run --repeat` or a loop through the Makefile).

## Tests

- vitest: the file above, repeated; a vitest for unmount during a pending save if the editor changes.

issues.title: Make the release test script fail loudly when its fixtures break
issues.body:
`tests/test-release.sh` failed once in CI on PR #174 (run 36755875472), in its very first case, 9 s into the job: three `fatal: not a git repository` lines, then `./tests/test-release.sh: line 68: ./release.sh: No such file or directory`. Every later case passed, and the same script has passed on every other run.

So the first case ran against a repository copy that was missing or incomplete. The script runs with `set -u` only: a failed `mktemp`, `cp -a` or `git init` while building or copying the fixtures goes unnoticed, and the case then fails with a confusing message instead of the real error.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fixture building and copying stop the script with the actual error when a step fails (check each step, or `set -e` in those functions).
- The cause of the missing copy is named if the error output shows it; otherwise the next failure will show it.
- The script still passes locally and in CI.

## Tests

- Shell: `tests/test-release.sh`, plus a deliberate failure (for example an unwritable temp dir) showing the new error.

issues.title: Move focus after comment posts once the target has rendered
issues.body:
#178 found that moving focus in a `requestAnimationFrame` after a comment save could run before React had re-rendered the target button, so focus was lost now and then (`comments.spec.ts` "edit, delete and the placeholder" failed 1 in 30 runs). It moved that one case into an effect that runs after the render.

The same wait-for-a-frame pattern is still used after posting a new thread and after posting a reply in `CommentsSection`, and possibly elsewhere in the web client.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every place that moves focus after a mutation does it after the element it targets is rendered (an effect keyed on the new state, or a ref callback), not in a frame callback.
- Keyboard users land on a predictable element after posting a thread or a reply.

## Tests

- vitest: focus after posting a thread and a reply.
- e2e: the comments specs with `REPEAT=50`.

issues.title: Let only authors and space admins delete comments
issues.body:
Since #176, anyone holding a space's `delete` permission may delete other people's comments. New spaces grant `delete` to everyone (#159), so by default every member can delete anyone's comment.

Decision by the product owner: deleting someone else's comment is moderation, not page housekeeping. The space `delete` permission keeps its meaning for pages (trash and restore) and no longer covers comments.

## Acceptance criteria

- Authors may delete their own comments, as now.
- Deleting another person's comment needs space administer. Space and organization admins hold it, as #19 defines. It is still audited as `comment.deleted`.
- The rule holds in the service and in the database: raw SQL as `stator_app` with a user set cannot delete or blank another person's comment without space administer.
- `ThreadCan` or `CommentCan` report the new rule, so the web shows Delete on other people's comments only to admins.
- docs/api-contract-m2.md and docs/decisions.md say so.

## Tests

- Integration: a member with `delete` but not administer is refused on someone else's comment through the API and through raw SQL; a space admin succeeds; the author succeeds.
- vitest: the Delete action follows the new flag.
- e2e: bob, a plain member, sees no Delete on alice's comment; a space admin does.

issues.title: Root out the flaky slash menu in the page blocks e2e spec
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/page-blocks.spec.ts:52` ("both blocks go in from the slash menu, and their links lead to the heading and the page", chromium) failed once in CI on PR #182 (run 36779476911), which only changed focus handling in the comment components; the rerun passed.

Failure: after typing `/`, `expect(page.getByRole("listbox", { name: "Insert a block" })).toBeVisible()` found no listbox. Likely suspects: the `/` was typed before the editor had focus or had finished mounting after navigation, or the slash menu opened and closed again because of a focus change.

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is named and fixed at its source; no retries or raised timeouts without a stated reason.
- The spec passes with `REPEAT=50` under the load of a parallel gate.

## Tests

- e2e: the spec above, repeated.

issues.title: Give the danger button AA contrast in dark mode
issues.body:
While building #27, the `danger` button variant failed axe colour contrast in dark mode (2.97:1 against its background), so the admin "Disconnect Armature" button was made `secondary` instead. Every other `danger` button (delete space, purge trash, delete comment, revoke token and so on) likely fails the same way in dark mode, and possibly in the Deep-Tech and Constellation themes.

issues.title: Give buttons type button by default so they never submit a form
issues.body:
Found while building #31: the bare `Button` in `web/src/components/ui` renders a `<button>` with no `type`, so the browser treats it as `type="submit"`. Inside the page editor's form, pressing such a button submits the form and opens Publish. #193 set `type="button"` on its new toolbar button only; the existing editor `ToolButton`s and "Copy heading link" (and possibly other buttons rendered inside a form) have the same problem.

issues.title: Fix flaky e2e test for following the Armature theme
issues.body:
"alice follows her Armature theme" in `e2e/armature-theme.spec.ts` (from #197) failed once in a full `./run-tests.sh` run on each of the #194 and #189 branches: after following, the page went back to the built-in accent. Both passed on rerun, so this looks like a race between the follow request and something that reapplies the stored theme (theme query refetch or ThemeLoader).

- e2e: the existing spec, repeated.

issues.title: Fix flaky replication fallback integration test
issues.body:
`TestALaggingConnectionFallsBackToThePrimary` in `backend/test/replication_test.go` failed once in the push gate for #201 on replication lag timing (411 ms against a 300 ms limit). The change under test did not touch replication; the next full run passed.

## Acceptance criteria

issues.title: Keep the create-issues e2e test well inside its timeout
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/create-issues.spec.ts` "alice files a sentence, a list and table rows as issues, and each gets its chip" timed out in CI on PR #205 (chromium, light: 21.9 s against the 20 s test timeout). In the same run the dark variant took 19.4 s and mobile 15.5 to 16.5 s, so the test runs right at its budget and any slow CI runner tips it over. PR #205 (find and replace) does not touch this flow.

## Acceptance criteria
- Find where the time goes (trace): slow steps, needless waits, or real slowness in the app (e.g. creating issues one by one, chip rendering).
- Fix the cause: make the app faster where it is slow, or split the test into focused tests (sentence, list, table rows) that each finish well inside the budget. Do not just raise the timeout.
- The spec passes 20 runs in a row with 4 workers.

## Tests
- e2e: the existing spec, repeated.

issues.title: Make the branch guard follow cd before git commands
issues.body:
`.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` resolves the checkout from the hook's `cwd` and from `git -C`, but ignores a `cd DIR` segment earlier in the same command. So `cd /path/to/worktree && git push` is judged against, and runs `./run-tests.sh` in, whatever checkout the shell started in, not the one being pushed.

Seen on PR #205: the push from a worktree returned at once, without the ~20 minute gate, and the branch then failed in CI. The same gap explains the earlier "gate ran in the wrong branch" surprises.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `cd DIR` (and `pushd DIR`) segment changes the directory that later segments in the same command are judged against, the way `git -C` already does; relative paths resolve against the current one.
- `cd DIR && git push` from a valid issue branch in a worktree runs `./run-tests.sh` in that worktree; from `main` it is refused.
- Edits, commits and merges after `cd DIR &&` are judged against DIR's branch.
- A `cd` the hook cannot resolve (variables, `~user`, command substitution) is judged conservatively: push is refused with a message to push without `cd` or with `git -C`.

## Tests
- `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`: cases for `cd worktree && git push`, `cd worktree; git commit`, `cd sub && cd .. && git push`, and an unresolvable `cd "$X" && git push`.

issues.title: Give e2e the same Biome formatter settings as web
issues.body:
`web/biome.json` holds the TypeScript style (2 spaces, 160 columns, double quotes, trailing commas), but `e2e/` has no Biome config. A Biome format run on an e2e file (for example by an editor or a format-on-save hook) falls back to Biome's defaults, tabs and 80 columns, and rewrites the whole file away from the repo's style. Seen while working on #206.

## Acceptance criteria
- One Biome config covers both `web/` and `e2e/` with the same settings (a root `biome.json` that `web/` extends, or an `e2e/biome.json` extending `web/`'s), with generated files still excluded.
- `biome format` on every existing file in `web/src` and `e2e/` changes nothing (the current code already follows the style), or any drift is fixed in the same PR.
- The gate checks it: `run-tests.sh` (via a Makefile target in a container) fails when a file in `web/` or `e2e/` is not formatted.

## Tests
- The new gate step itself; show it failing on a deliberately misformatted file before the fix lands.

issues.title: Log branch guard decisions to find skipped push gates
issues.body:
Twice an agent's `git push` from its worktree came back at once instead of after the ~20 minute `./run-tests.sh` gate (#205, and #212 after #209 landed). Replaying the exact command and cwd through the current `.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` shows it would run the gate in that worktree, so either the hook was not invoked, a different copy of it ran (for example the worktree's own `.claude/` if the project dir resolved to the worktree), or it exited early. Other pushes from worktrees did run the gate. CI still runs the full gate, so nothing reached main untested, but the local gate is meant to catch failures before a push.

## Acceptance criteria
- The hook appends one line per invocation to a log in the checkout's git common dir (for example `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/branch-guard.log`): time, hook path, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, cwd, tool, decision, and for pushes the checkout the gate ran in and how long it took. Command text is not logged beyond the git subcommand.
- The cause of the skipped gates is found with that log and fixed, or documented if it lies outside the repo (then report it upstream).
- `branch-guard-test.sh` covers the logging (a line is written for allow, deny and gate runs).

## Tests
- `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`.

issues.title: Clear the tooltip timer when the tooltip unmounts
issues.body:
`web/src/components/ui/Tooltip.tsx` starts a show timer on pointer enter or focus but never clears it when the tooltip unmounts. If the anchor goes away within `TOOLTIP_DELAY_MS` (navigation, a closing menu, the end of a test), the timer still calls `setShown` on an unmounted component. In vitest this surfaced as an unhandled `ReferenceError: window is not defined` after `Shell.test.tsx` tore down its environment, which fails the gate at random.

## Acceptance criteria
- The pending timer is cleared on unmount.
- A vitest test focuses a tooltip's anchor, unmounts before the delay, advances fake timers past it, and sees no state update or error.

issues.title: Find why an integration test cleanup hung until the suite timed out
issues.body:
In a push gate for #216 (a frontend-only change) the Go integration suite ran into the 10 minute `go test` timeout. The goroutine dump shows the cleanup of `harness.makeMember` (`backend/test/harness_test.go:201`) blocked in `pgxpool.Pool.Exec`, i.e. waiting on the database. The next run of the same commit passed the integration layer. The machine was running two other gates at the time (load about 13 on 12 cores).

## Acceptance criteria
- Find what the cleanup waited for: a lock held by another test's open transaction, a connection pool exhausted by leaked connections, or a replica wait. Capture `pg_stat_activity` / `pg_locks` when a test runs long (for example a watchdog in the harness that dumps them after N seconds, as a named constant).
- Fix the cause. Cleanup statements carry a context deadline so a stuck one fails that test with a clear message instead of hanging the whole package for 10 minutes.

## Tests
- Go integration: the harness watchdog and deadline are exercised by a test that holds a lock deliberately.

issues.title: Stop Chromium tabs crashing in the e2e layer of the gate
issues.body:
Chromium tabs crash now and then in the Playwright layer of the gate ("Target crashed"):
- `labels.spec.ts` during the #202 gate (worker SIGSEGV).
- `editor.spec.ts` "a swipe scrolls the slash menu and a tap picks from it" [mobile] during the #216 gate.

Both passed on the next run. The Playwright container already runs with `--ipc=host` and `--init`. Both times two or three gates ran at once on the host (31 GB RAM, about 19 GB in use), so memory pressure is a suspect.

## Acceptance criteria
- Find the cause: collect the crash reason (Chromium's `--enable-logging=stderr`, dmesg OOM killer lines, `docker stats` during a gate), and check worker count against available memory.
- Fix it, for example by sizing `WORKERS` from available memory, giving the container a memory limit that makes OOM visible instead of random, or by reducing per-test memory. Not by retrying crashed tests.
- Three gates run in parallel on this host without a tab crash in 10 consecutive attempts.

issues.title: Fix the load-sensitive table of contents vitest
issues.body:
`web/src/features/editor/pageBlocks.test.tsx` "keeps the table of contents up to date..." timed out once waiting for `[data-top-bar]` in the push gate for #217 (a backend-only change). The rerun passed. The host was under load from other gates at the time.

## Acceptance criteria
- Find why the test waits on `[data-top-bar]` at all and what makes it slow under load (a real timer, a lazy import, a fixed timeout in the test).
- Fix the cause so the test does not depend on host speed (fake timers, awaiting the right signal), not by raising its timeout.
- The file passes 50 runs in a row while `make test-go` runs beside it.

issues.title: Report that a home page cannot be trashed in the access inspector
issues.body:
The access inspector (#81, PR #225) reports "move to trash" from `perm_page_deletable`, but the database never lets a space's home page be trashed, and the page offers no such action. So for a home page the inspector can say a person may move it to the trash when nobody can. The integration test skips that one comparison.

## Acceptance criteria
- The inspector's answer for a home page says it cannot be moved to the trash, with the reason ("A space's home page cannot be moved to the trash"), derived from the same rule the database enforces (one SQL function both use), not a separate check in Go.
- The integration test compares the home page too, with no skip.

issues.title: Keep the people picker from picking a stale match on Enter
issues.body:
The people picker keeps showing the previous results while it fetches results for the new text. Pressing Enter right after typing can pick the person who was first for the old text. Seen while writing the keyboard e2e test for #81; the test waits for the right person to be first, the picker is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- While results for the current text are loading, the list does not offer stale matches for Enter: either Enter waits for the current results, or stale entries are marked and not selectable.
- A screen reader hears that results are loading.

## Tests
- vitest: type, press Enter before the new results arrive, the right person (or nobody) is picked.
- e2e: the keyboard flow in the access inspector no longer needs to wait for the list.

issues.title: Fix four load and timer flakes in vitest and e2e
issues.body:
Found while working on #218 and #223 (PRs #229, #224); each passes alone but fails under load or by timing:

1. **Parallel gates and vitest workers.** Three gates starting together gave 24 failures from vitest's default 5 s test timeout in one round: each run starts a worker per core on the same 12 cores. Bound vitest's workers (for example from a named constant or from the cores not already busy) so parallel gates do not starve each other; do not just raise the timeout.
2. **`Editor.test.tsx` "heading anchors ... copied as a link".** A real timer clears the "Link copied" status before the assertion reads it. Use fake timers or assert on the right signal.
3. **`templates.test.tsx`.** A router timer fires after the test environment is torn down (`window is not defined`). Find the timer and clean it up on unmount (the same class of bug as #216).
4. **`status-date-emoji.spec.ts` axe tests.** They went over the 20 s Playwright timeout under load. Find where the time goes (as #206 did) and split or speed up; do not raise the timeout.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each cause found and fixed at its source, one commit each.
- Each affected file passes 30 runs in a row with `make test-go TESTFLAGS=-count=1` looping beside it; three gates started 2 minutes apart pass.

issues.title: Fix the reply editor focus race in the mobile comments e2e test
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/comments.spec.ts:193` "the comments are accessible and keyboard usable in dark" [mobile] failed in CI on PR #234 (audit log, unrelated): `expect(locator).toBeFocused()` on the reply editor (`role=textbox`, `aria-label="Your reply to ..."`) did not hold across 11 retries. The same class of race was fixed for other editors in #179 (rAF focus) and #184 (ProseMirror restoring the selection after focus).

## Acceptance criteria
- Find what takes focus away from the reply editor (or never gives it) on the mobile project: a late ProseMirror selection restore, a scroll-into-view, the virtual keyboard emulation, or a re-render that replaces the node.
- Fix the cause in the app (or the test's interaction if it does something a person would not), not with a longer timeout.
- The spec passes 30 runs in a row on the mobile project with 4 workers.

issues.title: Restore sharing and the reply focus fix undone by the archive merge
issues.body:
The archive PR #239 landed as one commit, e852585, whose tree was built on main as of #236 (db94548) instead of on its real parent 402a5e7. Merging it silently undid the two PRs that had landed in between:

issues.title: Fix flaky verification and audit e2e tests
issues.body:
Two e2e specs blocked push gates for #240 (stale report) and passed on rerun and in isolation:

1. `e2e/tests/verification.spec.ts` "bob, who may only read..." on the mobile project (from #68).

issues.title: Fix the image tag race and two load-sensitive vitest files
issues.body:
Gate failures seen while pushing #110 (webhooks), unrelated to it, each passing on rerun:

1. **Docker image tagging race during stack start.** `docker compose up --build` failed while tagging an image; looks like two services building or tagging the same image name at once (or two gates sharing an image name). ## Acceptance criteria
- Each cause found and fixed at its source, no raised timeouts or retries.
- Three gates started 2 minutes apart pass; each vitest file passes 30 runs with `make test-go TESTFLAGS=-count=1` looping beside.

issues.title: Refuse two Go types that map to one OpenAPI schema name
issues.body:
Found while building #97 (PR #248): two Go types with the same name in different packages (`Stats` for readiness and a new `Stats` for page views) collapse into one schema name in `api/openapi.json`. The builder silently keeps one and drops the other, so a route documents the wrong body and `schema.d.ts` types the client wrong, with no error.

## Acceptance criteria
- The OpenAPI builder (backend/internal/openapi, the spec builder used by the route table) fails generation with a clear message naming both Go types when two different types map to one schema name, unless an explicit override names them apart.
- A unit test proves the failure with two same-named types from two packages.
- `make openapi` on main still produces the same document (no existing collision), or any found is fixed in the same PR.

issues.title: Fix the flaky restricted-page test in the stars and home e2e spec
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/stars-home.spec.ts:101` "a page restricted away from bob leaves his stars and his updates" (mobile project, from #38) failed once in the push gate for #252 and passed on the rerun.

## Acceptance criteria
- Find the cause from the trace (read-after-write on a replica after the restriction, a cached home query not refetched, a race in the test's own steps) and fix it in the app or the test, not with a longer timeout or retries.

issues.title: Link card axe test scans the embedded video player's own markup

## Problem

`link cards pass axe in light/dark` (e2e/tests/link-previews.spec.ts) fails in CI on main and on every pull request, in both the chromium and mobile projects.
