issues.title: fix(db): migrations run as a non-superuser owner miss rows behind row security
issues.body:
An instance installed by the chart with CloudNativePG cannot upgrade past 00660:

```
ERROR 00670_example_renewal.sql: ... ERROR: check constraint "space_example_versioned" of relation "space" is violated by some row (SQLSTATE 23514)
```

**Why:** with CNPG the migrate job runs as the owner role `stator_owner`, which is not a superuser and has no BYPASSRLS. `space` has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and, before 00750, the tenant policy `org_id = current_org_id()`. The migration sets no `app.org_id`, so its backfill `UPDATE space ... WHERE example` sees no row and updates none, and the CHECK added next fails on every example space. In compose and CI the migrations run as the superuser, and the chart's install-and-upgrade test starts from an empty database, so nothing caught it.

The same applies to every data-changing statement in a migration before 00750 that reads or writes a table with forced row security: a backfill that silently does nothing, an `INSERT ... SELECT` that copies nothing, or a check like 00740's count of organizations that sees none.

**What to do:**
- Make every such statement independent of the role that runs it, e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` around the backfill and `FORCE` again after it (the owner then bypasses its own policies), in 00670 and every other affected migration. Editing applied migrations is safe here: an instance past them never runs them again, and one stuck before them needs exactly this.
- A test that runs the whole migration chain as a non-superuser owner without BYPASSRLS (as CNPG does) against a database with data from the oldest supported release: several spaces including an example space, pages, attachments, themes, tokens; and checks every backfill reached its rows. Ideally the chart's upgrade test in kind upgrades a seeded instance too.
- docs/upgrading or the release notes: the workaround for an instance that already hit this (below).

**Workaround for a stuck instance** (each migration runs in its own transaction, so the failed one left nothing behind):
```
kubectl exec -n <ns> <cluster>-1 -- psql -c 'ALTER ROLE stator_owner BYPASSRLS'
# run the upgrade again (helm upgrade, or delete the failed migrate job so it reruns)
kubectl exec -n <ns> <cluster>-1 -- psql -c 'ALTER ROLE stator_owner NOBYPASSRLS'
```

issues.title: feat(webhook): offer envelope version 2 in the CloudEvents shape
issues.body:
Armature, Stator and Exciter send webhooks in one shared envelope, version 1: `{version, id, topic, occurredAt, payload}` plus `source`. Version 2 follows the CloudEvents 1.0 specification, so any receiver, a future relay in Dynamo, or a standard broker understands it without tool-specific code.

- Structured mode (`application/cloudevents+json`): `specversion: "1.0"`, `id`, `source` (e.g. `/armature`, `/stator`, `/exciter`, or the instance's URL), `type` (e.g. `dev.armature.issue.updated`, `dev.stator.page.remote_link.removed`), `time`, `datacontenttype: "application/json"`, `data` (the version 1 payload), and the extension attribute `dataversion` for the payload's own version.
- Signatures stay as in version 1 (HMAC over the body, timestamped signature header), since CloudEvents leaves authentication to the transport.
- An endpoint chooses the version it receives when it is registered; version 1 stays the default and keeps working for at least one Dynamo release after version 2 ships. The receiver side accepts both.
- Event types are listed with their payloads in the tool's OpenAPI document (or a schema beside it) and in Dynamo's shared list (praetorianer777/Dynamo#4).
- Events stay thin: ids, keys and what changed, no content a subscriber's own rights might not cover.
- Capability `webhooks@2` in `/api/v1/meta` once supported, next to `webhooks@1`.

issues.title: feat: Exciter requirements as chips and blocks on pages
issues.body:
Exciter wants its requirements shown live on Stator pages, as Stator shows Armature's issues: a chip for a key such as `CHK-R42`, a block with one requirement, and a block listing the requirements a query finds. Exciter's side is Cloudster1/Exciter#43. The agreement is in Exciter's `docs/api-contract-backlog.md`, section "#43 Exciter requirements in Stator pages" (Cloudster1/Exciter#140).

**What to build in Stator**

- **An Exciter connection.**
  - An administrator saves Exciter's origin, which answers `product: "exciter"` at `GET /api/v1/meta`.
  - Each member stores their own Exciter personal access token (`exciter_pat_`; a read-only token is enough). Every read is made with the viewer's token, as Armature reads are.
  - Before offering each feature, Stator checks Exciter's capabilities by exact name: `requirement-embed@1`, `requirement-list@1`, `specifications@1` and `webhooks@1`.
- **Chips.**
  - A requirement key (`^([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9})-R([1-9][0-9]*)$`) written or picked on a page becomes a chip. It is read with `GET /requirements/{reqKey}` and shows the title, status and revision. It links to `{exciter}/p/{projectKey}/r/{key}`.
  - A former key still reads, and the answer carries the current `key`.
  - A requirement the reader may not see is 404. Without a token, the reader sees the key as a link and how to connect.
- **A requirement block.**
  - It shows one requirement with its statement and rationale. Both are ProseMirror documents in Exciter's schema; render what Stator knows and show the rest as text.
  - The picker uses `GET /search/quick`.
- **A list block.**
  - It holds a project, picked from `GET /projects`, and a query in Exciter's query language.
  - It reads `GET /projects/{projectKey}/requirements?query=&limit=&offset=` as the viewer and shows key, title, status and revision, a window at a time (`limit` up to 500, with `total` for paging).
  - `currentUser()` means the viewer, so the same block can read differently to different readers.
  - A query that does not parse is `400 bad_query`, with `position` giving the offending character.
  - The editor completes at the caret from `GET /projects/{projectKey}/requirements/suggest?q=&at=`.
- **Cache and freshness.**
  - Answers are cached per viewer for at most 60 seconds.
  - An Exciter administrator adds an Exciter webhook for Stator's receiver, with the topics `requirement.created`, `requirement.revised`, `requirement.changed`, `requirement.trashed`, `requirement.restored`, `requirement.moved` and `review.decided`, and Stator stores its `exciter_whs_` secret.
  - Deliveries come in envelope version 1 with `source: "exciter"`, signed in `X-Exciter-Signature-256`, and name the requirement by `id` and `key`. They only clear the cache: the payload is read as the webhook's owner, so it is never shown.

**Not asked for:** writing to Exciter from a page, or an embed format such as oEmbed. Page links between requirements and pages (Exciter #41 and #42, on Stator's remote links) stay as they are; a chip does not make a page link.

issues.title: feat(oauth): let partner tools and assistants connect to the MCP endpoint with OAuth 2.1
issues.body:
Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor#1), the workflow backplane for Stator, Armature and Exciter, runs workflows that read and write Stator pages as the person who started them. Today Stator's `/api/v1/mcp` accepts only personal access tokens, so a person would have to paste a long-lived token into Rotor. Exciter already solved this with its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server (Cloudster1/Exciter#188), and Exciter's MCP contract (Cloudster1/Exciter#182) asks the tools to share one approach.

- An authorization server as in Cloudster1/Exciter#188: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata for `/api/v1/mcp` and `WWW-Authenticate` on a 401, RFC 8414 metadata, PKCE `S256`, RFC 7591 registration or a client metadata document, `resource` (RFC 8707), revocation (RFC 7009)
- Refresh tokens rotate at each use; one used twice ends the grant; access tokens last at most an hour
- Scopes for reading and for writing pages, and the space limits a personal token already offers; an issued token never exceeds the person's rights
- OAuth access tokens are accepted at `/api/v1/mcp` and nowhere else
- Writes made through a connected app are marked with that app, as Exciter's `via` does (Cloudster1/Exciter#190)
- Optional but wanted by Rotor: RFC 8693 token exchange so a connected app can take a narrower, shorter access token without narrowing its grant (the same request as the Exciter issue linked from Cloudster1/Rotor#12)
- Capability `oauth.partner-tokens@1` in `GET /api/v1/meta`

This is the counterpart of #428, which consumes Armature's server; it would fit the milestone "M9 Automation and AI". It blocks Cloudster1/Rotor#45.

issues.title: test(load): measure resources against generated data sets for sizing
issues.body:
## Goal

Say what hardware an installation needs for a given amount of content and number of people, from measurements instead of guesses, and set the chart's resource defaults from them.

The load test of #368 seeds one space of 2,000 pages. A real installation grows to many spaces, hundreds of thousands of page versions and gigabytes of attachments, and much of the cost of a request grows with that: the page tree, search, permission checks, backlinks, version history, exports and backups all read more rows, and Postgres needs more memory to keep its working set cached. A load level that holds on 2,000 pages says little about one with 200,000.

## Scope

- **A generator for large data sets**, run by `make load-seed LOAD_SIZE=<size>`, writing straight through the API or a bulk path that keeps every invariant the API keeps (permissions, versions, search index, links). Sizes, roughly:

  | Size | Spaces | Pages | Versions per page | Members | Comments | Attachments |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `small` | 10 | 2,000 | 3 | 20 | 2,000 | 500 MB |
  | `medium` | 100 | 50,000 | 8 | 500 | 50,000 | 10 GB |
  | `large` | 500 | 250,000 | 15 | 5,000 | 250,000 | 50 GB |

  Spaces are not all the same size: most are small, a few are large, and each size has some very large spaces, because the tree, search within a space, space permissions and space exports grow with the pages of one space rather than with the whole installation. Roughly:

  | Size | Very large spaces | Large spaces | The rest |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `small` | 1 of 1,000 pages | 3 of 200 | spread over the others |
  | `medium` | 3 of 15,000 pages | 10 of 2,000 | spread over the others |
  | `large` | 4 of 50,000 pages | 20 of 3,000 | spread over the others |

  Several large spaces at once matter too: their trees, indexes and permission sets compete for the same Postgres cache, which one large space alone does not show.

  The scenarios run against the largest space and against a typical one, and the results name which.

  **Pages are filled as people fill them**, since an empty page costs nothing to render, index, version or export. The mix is drawn per page, from a short note to a long reference page:

  - text: paragraphs, headings, lists, task lists, quotes, links to other pages and anchors, inline comments, mentions, emoji, inline values;
  - tables, some large (hundreds of rows), some with merged cells;
  - images and other attachments of realistic sizes and types (photos, screenshots, PDFs, office files), some with several versions, some shown in galleries;
  - diagrams, code blocks in several languages, expand and column layouts, panels and decisions;
  - includes and excerpts of other pages, child page lists, blog posts and calendars;
  - Armature issue chips, blocks and lists against the stub, so reading such a page does what it does in production.

  **Content comes from free sources on the internet**, so text, structure and pictures look like real ones:

  - text and page structure from a pinned Wikipedia dump (articles bring headings, tables, lists and links between pages), in English and German so search meets both;
  - public domain books from Project Gutenberg for long pages;
  - pictures and PDFs from CC0 or public domain collections (for example NASA, or museum open access collections), in the sizes and formats people upload;
  - code from permissively licensed repositories for code blocks.

  `make load-corpus` downloads it once into a cache outside the repository, pinned by URL and SHA-256 in a committed manifest, so every run uses the same content and CI does not depend on the sources being up. Only the manifest is committed, never the content; each source and its licence is listed in it. The generator falls back to generated text and pictures when the cache is missing, so the smoke profile runs offline.

  Realistic shape: page sizes and tree depth spread as in real wikis, links between pages, restricted spaces and pages, groups, templates, labels. Deterministic from a seed, so two runs make the same data.
- **The existing scenarios run against each size**, with the same profiles, so latency and throughput can be compared across sizes as well as across load.
- **Resource use recorded per run**: CPU and memory of api, web, render and Postgres, Postgres connections, cache hit ratio, database and attachment size on disk, backup and restore duration, export duration of the largest space and of a typical one.
- **A sizing table in `docs/sizing.md`**: per size and load level the CPU, memory and disk to give each component, disk growth per 1,000 pages and per GB of attachments, and the point where a component needs more before latency suffers.
- **Chart defaults** in `values.yaml` updated to the smallest measured size, with the larger ones as documented examples.

## Not in scope

- Fixing what it finds; each slow query or limit becomes an issue of its own, as with #370 and #371.

## Done when

- `small` and `medium` are measured locally and in kind; `large` is measured once, on hardware described in the doc.
- `docs/sizing.md` holds the table and how it was measured, and `docs/load-testing.md` links to it.

Related: #368, #378, #381.

issues.title: A suite demo with a user guide and the docs of Armature, Exciter, Stator and Rotor
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Stator together with Armature, Exciter and Rotor, I want a suite demo whose spaces hold a user guide for every function of each tool and each tool's own documentation, so that I learn the suite from the suite and see the tools working on real, linked content.

Part of one suite demo: Armature holds the issues (Cloudster1/Armature#300, Rotor in Cloudster1/Armature#486), Stator the documentation and Exciter the requirements and tests (Cloudster1/Exciter#488), and Exciter traces between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Adding it:** an administrator adds the suite demo once, beside the example space, and `make seed` adds it too. It is refused when one of its keys is taken.
- [ ] **Spaces:** four spaces, `ARM`, `EXC`, `STA` and `ROT`, each with two trees: **User guide** and **Developer docs**.
- [ ] **User guide:** hand-written pages, in English and German, the reader's language chosen as for the example space. One page per function area, covering every function the tool has today: what it is for, how to do it step by step, who may do it, and how it works with the other tools. The `STA` guide is the example space's guides, not a second copy of them; pages are added only for what they leave out. The `ROT` guide says plainly that Rotor has not released yet.
- [ ] **Developer docs:** the README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG and every Markdown file under `docs/` of the tool's repository, in its folder tree. Images become attachments.
- [ ] **Decisions:** `docs/decisions.md` becomes a page with one child page per top-level section, so no page is too long to read or edit.
- [ ] **Links between docs:** links between docs become page links, also across tools (a GitHub link from Exciter's docs to Armature's `docs/integration.md` opens that page in `ARM`). Links to source files point at GitHub, at the snapshot's commit.
- [ ] **Issue references:** `#261` in Exciter's docs and `Cloudster1/Armature#213` anywhere become issue chips (`EXC-261`, `ARM-213`). They resolve once Armature has its suite demo, and publishing puts the page links on those issues.
- [ ] **Labels for partners:** every page carries a label naming its source (`demo-exc-guide-baselines`, `demo-exc-docs-api-contract-m13`), so Exciter finds it through `GET /labels/{name}/pages`.
- [ ] **Snapshot:** the developer docs come from a snapshot in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network. `make demo-snapshot` refreshes it from the four repositories and records the date and commit of each.

## Tests

- Go unit: link and reference rewriting (relative, cross-tool, source files, `#N` and `owner/repo#N`); splitting the decisions; label names; every guide page exists in both languages under the same name.
- Integration: add the demo; a second add and a taken key are refused; the page trees match the content; a cross-space page link and an issue chip are present.
- vitest: the control that adds the demo.
- Playwright: add the demo, open a guide page, a decisions page and a page with a chip, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- Follows `backend/internal/example`: embedded content, a worker job that builds through the services as a person would, and `versions.json` for renewal. The guides use the example space's front matter and block markers.
- The folder import of `internal/mdio`.
- A decision in `docs/decisions.md`: why a snapshot and not git sync.

## Depends on

- Nothing to build. The chips resolve with Cloudster1/Armature#300.

issues.title: feat(oauth): hand partner tools a person's token by token exchange
issues.body:
Exciter reads Stator pages and puts links on them as each person. Stator should hand Exciter a person's token from that person's Keycloak sign-in, as Armature does since Cloudster1/Armature#280, so nobody pastes a `stator_pat_` into Exciter.

- `POST /api/v1/oauth/token` with the token-exchange grant (RFC 8693): it takes an access token of Stator's OIDC provider whose `azp` is a registered partner app's Keycloak client id and whose `aud` holds Stator's client, the app authenticating with its client id and secret.
- Partner apps registered by an administrator: `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/oauth/clients` with `{name, scopes, keycloakClientId}`, secrets `stator_ocs_...` shown once.
- The person is matched by verified email; a person not yet in Stator is admitted only by Stator's group mapping (if new people in a mapped group are not admitted at sign-in today, make that so too, behind a setting). The token never exceeds the person's rights.
- Tokens issued this way show in the person's token list as "<app> (connected app)", revocable there; revoking ends the refresh token.
- Discovery at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and capability `oauth.token-exchange@1` in `GET /api/v1/meta`, with the same promise as Armature's.


Part of the connected deployment from [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo): the three tools share one Keycloak realm (`dynamo`), a person signs in to whichever tool they open, and the tools connect that person to each other without a click or a pasted token. Dynamo only tests the combination and ships an umbrella chart whose setup job wires the tools once through their admin APIs.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: feat(exciter): connect people to Exciter at sign-in with shared login
issues.body:
Stator reads Exciter requirements on pages as each viewer (#440), with an `exciter_pat_` each member pastes. Connect people to Exciter at sign-in instead, as Stator does toward Armature (#430).

- After an OIDC sign-in, Stator exchanges the person's Keycloak access token at Exciter's `POST /api/v1/oauth/token` (token exchange, RFC 8693, Exciter's side is Cloudster1/Exciter#273), stores the tokens sealed and the worker refreshes them.
- Stator is registered in Exciter as a partner app with its Keycloak client id; the administrator stores its client id and secret on the Exciter connection.
- On only when the operator enables it: `STATOR_EXCITER_TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, Helm `exciter.tokenExchange`, and only when Exciter reports `oauth.token-exchange@1`.
- A failed exchange never fails the sign-in; the profile says why Exciter is not connected. The pasted token stays as the fallback.
- Also: `STATOR_EXCITER_WEBHOOK_URL` (Helm `exciter.webhookUrl`), the receiver address Stator names for Exciter's webhook, as `STATOR_ARMATURE_WEBHOOK_URL` does for Armature, so a cluster can give Exciter an in-network address.


Part of the connected deployment from [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo): the three tools share one Keycloak realm (`dynamo`), a person signs in to whichever tool they open, and the tools connect that person to each other without a click or a pasted token. Dynamo only tests the combination and ships an umbrella chart whose setup job wires the tools once through their admin APIs.

issues.title: Split the avatar menu: personal pages there, administration in a settings area
issues.body:
The three tools that run together (Stator, Armature, Exciter) are moving to one menu layout, described in praetorianer777/Dynamo#12: personal pages under the avatar, administration in a settings area of its own, the sidebar for work. Stator keeps its avatar menu but splits it: today personal and administrator pages sit in one flat dropdown, and the space has no admin group. This is Stator's part.

## Top bar goes
- The quick-search button and the waiting-reviews button are removed.
- The avatar and its menu move to the bottom of the rail.
- On narrow screens, a thin strip with "Open the navigation" stays.
- The notification bell moves to the rail, after Search. Its panel stays as it is.

## Rail
- In order: toggle, Home, Hub (configured, not for guests), Search, Notifications (bell), Spaces (not for guests), My tasks.
- Bottom: the theme switch and the avatar.

## Avatar menu
The avatar opens the menu, folded or not. It keeps only what is about the person:
- A header with name, email and role.
- Your profile, Notification settings, Watching, Themes, Access tokens (not for guests), in this order.
- The connected tools (#494).
- **Settings**, for site administrators only, opening the settings area.
- Sign out.

Every administrator page leaves the menu: Single sign-on, Permissions, Hub page, Templates, Stale pages, Example space, Export brand, Export and import, Armature, Exciter, Webhooks, Audit log.

## Settings area
`/settings` and the pages under it get a sidebar of their own in place of the wiki's, headed by "Back to Stator", which returns to the last page outside it.
- **You:** Your profile, Notification settings, Watching, Themes, Access tokens, then Armature account and Exciter account.
- **Settings**, for site administrators only, in this order:
  - Single sign-on (with its join-request badge)
  - Permissions
  - Hub page
  - Templates
  - Stale pages
  - Example space
  - Export brand
  - Export and import
  - Armature
  - Exciter
  - Webhooks
  - Audit log

The whole group and the avatar menu's Settings use `useCanAdministerSite()`. Today Single sign-on checks the role while the rest check access, so the two can disagree.

`/settings` itself becomes a hub page with a "You" card and a "Settings" card for site administrators. The "Settings" breadcrumb, which links nowhere today, links to it.

## Sidebar
**Wiki group:** Home, Hub, Search, Reviews (`/reviews`, carrying the waiting count that was the top-bar button), My tasks, Spaces.

**Space group:**
- Starts with a space switcher, like Armature's project switcher and Exciter's.
- Then Space home, shortcuts, the page tree, Blog and Decisions.
- When the route names no space, the last one visited is shown.
- A nested "Space admin" group, folded by default, holds:
  - Space settings
  - Trash (`can.deletePages`)
  - Archive
  - Stale pages for the space (`can.administer`)

No personal and no site settings pages in the sidebar. **Foot:** the build stamp.

## Palette
The palette (QuickSearch) keeps its page results and also offers every page of the sidebar, the avatar menu and the settings area, filtered by the same rules. Exciter's `features/shell/places.ts` is a model for one registry they all read.

## Done when
- The avatar menu holds personal pages, the connected tools, Settings for site administrators and Sign out, and no administrator page.
- Every administrator page is reachable from the settings area and the palette, and from neither for a member.
- A guest sees no Hub, Spaces, Access tokens or Settings.
- The e2e suite checks the avatar menu and the settings area for a site administrator, a member and a guest, and the drawer at phone width.

issues.title: Use the suite's shared names for menu entries

issues.title: Find out whether Kroki can draw PlantUML and other diagram languages
issues.body:
Authors want more diagram languages than Mermaid. PlantUML and BPMN are the usual requests, and others include C4 (Structurizr), Graphviz, D2, ditaa, Vega and WaveDrom. [Kroki](https://kroki.io) draws all of these through one HTTP API: `POST /{language}/svg` with the diagram's text. It is self-hostable and MIT-licensed.

This issue is to find out whether Stator should use it. The outcome is a decision, not the feature.

## Where Stator stands
- **Mermaid** (#46) is drawn in each reader's browser. The diagram block holds Mermaid text (`document.NodeDiagram`), readers see SVG in the page's colours, and Markdown export writes a `mermaid` fence.
- **Sketches** (#312, #325) are an Excalidraw canvas, edited live together. The page stores the scene.
- Nothing is drawn on the server today. Anything new that is drawn on the server has to go out through the outbound guard (`STATOR_OUTBOUND_ALLOW`), as link previews do.

## Questions to answer
1. **Languages:** which ones do authors actually need? Each Kroki language is either built into the main image or needs a companion container (mermaid, bpmn, excalidraw, diagramsnet). Which do we need, and what does each cost to run?
2. **Self-hosted only:** sending page content to kroki.io is not acceptable.
   - Can Kroki and the companions it needs run in the compose stack and the Helm chart, reached only inside the installation?
   - How much CPU and memory do they need? The mermaid and bpmn companions run a headless browser.
   - Kroki becomes another service in Dynamo's deployment, so one Kroki could also serve Armature and Exciter.
3. **Security:**
   - PlantUML `!include` and URL fetches: does `KROKI_SAFE_MODE=secure` close them?
   - What does Stator have to do to the returned SVG before it is put in a page? Sanitize it, or show it as an image only?
   - How large may a diagram's text be, and how long may it take to draw?
4. **Where drawing happens:**
   - Drawn when the page is saved, so the SVG is stored or cached in Valkey keyed by a hash of the text?
   - Or drawn when the page is read?
   - What does a reader see when Kroki is down?
   - Must PDF and Word export work without Kroki?
5. **Mermaid and Excalidraw:**
   - Should Mermaid stay in the browser? That keeps the live preview, the page's colours and offline drawing.
   - Or move to Kroki for one path for every language?
   - Kroki can turn an Excalidraw scene into SVG. Is that any use for export, given the canvas already draws itself?
6. **Editing:**
   - How does an author get a live preview without a round trip per keystroke? For example, debounced requests through the api.
   - How does the block say why a diagram cannot be drawn, as the Mermaid block does?
7. **Storage and export:**
   - Does the diagram node grow a `language` attribute next to the text?
   - How do Markdown export and import write and read fences (`plantuml`, `bpmn`, ...)?
   - Do search and the document allowlist need changes?

## Done when
- A decision record in `docs/decisions` answers the questions above. It says yes, no, or yes for a named set of languages, with the measured cost of running Kroki and its companions.
- If yes, there are follow-up issues for the block, the server side, the compose and Helm services, and for Dynamo's deployment.
- A short throwaway spike (Kroki in compose and one PlantUML diagram drawn through the api) may back the decision. It is not merged.

issues.title: Stop the one-click Armature connection test from failing by chance
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/armature-connected-app.spec.ts:114` › "connecting Armature with one click › a member waits for an Armature administrator to allow a pending app" fails by chance.

```
TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('[data-action="connect-armature-app"]')
> 117 |     await bob.locator('[data-action="connect-armature-app"]').click();
```

**Where it was seen:**
- main's nightly run of 2026-10-20 (test-e2e 1/4).
- Local runs of #430, #461 and #462 (at both desktop and phone width).
- It passed when rerun every time.

**Likely cause:** bob's page is still showing the connection state from before the administrator stored the app, and nothing makes it fetch again. Clicking by a fixed timeout then races that state. The test should wait for what makes the button appear rather than for 5 s.

## Done when
- The test passes 20 times in a row on a loaded machine. For example, run `npx playwright test <file> --repeat-each=20` against the running stack, or the CI job by hand (`workflow_dispatch`).
- It still fails when the behaviour it checks is broken.
- A longer timeout or a retry alone does not count as the fix.

> 102 |     await expect(dialog(bob).locator("[data-template-preview] [data-template-variable=customer]")).toBeVisible();

issues.title: Stop the file versions test from fulfilling a disposed request
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/attachment-versions.spec.ts:95` › "file versions › a file uploaded while the list is still loading appears" fails by chance.

```
Error: route.fulfill: Fetch response has been disposed
    at /src/e2e/tests/attachment-versions.spec.ts:104:19
Error: browserContext.close: Test ended.
```

**Where it was seen:** two of four local browser runs of #430 (chromium). It passed in the others.

**Likely cause:** the test holds the attachment list's request with `page.route` to keep the list loading, then fulfils it. When the page refetches or cancels that request first, the held response is disposed and `route.fulfill` throws. The route should fulfil the request it actually holds, for example by keeping the `Route` and fetching inside the handler, or the test should gate on something the page awaits.

issues.body:
`e2e/tests/exciter.spec.ts:234` › "Exciter requirements on pages › an author inserts a requirement block and a list, completing the query at the caret" fails by chance.

```
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
  - waiting for getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Insert an Exciter requirement list' }).getByRole('option', { name: 'Approved' })
> 267 |     await expect(dialog.getByRole("option", { name: "Approved" })).toBeVisible();
```

issues.title: Stop the release test's fixture from racing a background git gc
issues.body:
`tests/test-release.sh` fails by chance in the shell layer:

```
rm: cannot remove '/tmp/tmp.uKnMI6YrGw/repo.remote': Directory not empty
❌ The test fixture broke while removing the previous case's repository.
```

**Where it was seen:** CI on #467 ("shell and format"). It passed locally and in the same job on the other PRs.

**Likely cause:** each case pushes to a throwaway bare repository (line 71), and `git push` can start `git gc --auto` in the background. The next case's `rm -rf "${REPO}" "${REPO}.remote"` (line 79) then races that gc still writing into `repo.remote`. The fix is to turn background gc off in the fixture's repositories, with `gc.auto=0`, or `gc.autoDetach=false` where gc has to run. Turning it off means every git call the test makes is finished by the time the next case starts.

## Done when
- `tests/test-release.sh` passes 50 times in a row in the shell layer's container.
- No case leaves a git process running behind it.

issues.title: Stop the real Armature installation test from reading a stale replica
issues.body:
`e2e/real-armature/connect.spec.ts:165` › "the first token that checks out teaches Stator the installation, by the id Armature names" fails by chance in the test-armature layer:

```
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
Locator: getByText(/confirmed its installation through a member's token/)
> 173 |     await expect(page.getByText(/confirmed its installation through a member's token/)).toBeVisible();
```

**Where it was seen:** CI on #467, whose change cannot reach this spec (it only touches a Go integration test and `mk/go.mk`).

**Cause:** the same as #471. The test polls `GET /armature/connection` until the installation id shows. The page it opens next reads through another session, which can hit a replica that has not replayed that write yet. So the page still shows the connection from before the token checked out.

**Fix:** open `/settings/armature` with `openShowing` (`e2e/fixtures/replica.ts`), waiting for the sentence. This is the suite's convention for a read after a write in another session.

## Done when
- The spec passes 20 times in a row against a real Armature, for example with `make test-armature ONLY="teaches Stator the installation" REPEAT=20`.
- It still fails when the sentence is never shown.

issues.title: Give the PDF brand test's print request the print budget
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/pdf-brand.spec.ts:12` › "the organization's logo and footer line are on the sheet the PDF is printed from, and the logo is in the file" fails by chance:

```
TimeoutError: apiRequestContext.fetch: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
  - → GET http://localhost:24900/api/v1/pages/<id>/pdf
   at ../fixtures/api.ts:16
```

**Where it was seen:**
- The local gate for #452, on a machine also running another stack.
- One of #430's local browser runs.
- Both passed when rerun.

**Cause:** the `api` fixture (`e2e/fixtures/api.ts`) sends every request through Playwright's `APIRequestContext` with its default 5 s timeout. `GET /pages/{id}/pdf` prints the page through the render service, which can take longer than that under load. The test gives printing 30 s (`PRINTED`), but that only bounds the locators and the `expect.poll`, not the request inside `pdf()`. So one slow print fails the test, although Stator answered correctly.

**Fix:** a request that prints should get the print budget, not 5 s. For example, the fixture could take a per-request timeout, or `pdf()` could fetch with `PRINTED.timeout`. That budget should stay below the server's own render timeout, so that a print the server gives up on still fails the test with Stator's answer. A shorter 5 s default for everything else is right as it is.

## Done when
- The spec passes 20 times in a row on a loaded machine (`make test-e2e ONLY="the brand in a PDF" REPEAT=20` while another stack runs).
- A print that never finishes still fails it.

issues.title: Let release.sh cut a release with a long commit history
issues.body:
`./release.sh --dry-run` (and `./release.sh 0.1.0`) fail on `main` before anything is written:

```
./release.sh: line 194: /usr/bin/python3: Argument list too long
./release.sh: line 386: /usr/bin/date: Argument list too long
```

**Cause:** the commits since the last tag reach Python as the environment variable `RAW_LOG`. Before the first tag that's the whole history, 958 commits or about 435 KB, and Linux refuses any single environment string over 128 KB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`). So every program started with it fails, the version inference and the notes alike. The release commit's message also goes through `-m "$(cat notes)"`; at about 106 KB of notes it's just under that same limit.

**Fix:** write the log to a temporary file and give Python its path; commit with `-F`. Then no step depends on how long the history or the notes are. Exciter's `release.sh` has the same code, and Armature's `deploy/release.sh` may too.

## Done when
- `./release.sh --dry-run` works on `main`.
- `tests/test-release.sh` has a case whose history is far over 128 KB.

issues.title: Run the static layers while the gate's stack starts
issues.body:
The local full gate (`./run-tests.sh` with no arguments, which the branch guard runs) takes about 43 minutes, and it runs every layer one after another. The last run:

| Layer | Time |
| --- | --- |
| shell | 3:02 |
| check-format | 0:07 |
| check-go | 2:17 |
| check-web | 4:11 |
| stack-up | 2:49 |
| test-integration | 10:31 |
| test-backup | 0:35 |
| test-e2e | 17:11 |
| test-armature | 1:14 |

`shell`, `check-format`, `check-go` and `check-web` need no stack, yet the stack only starts once they've finished.

**Change:** start `stack-up` first, in the background, run the four static layers while it comes up, and wait for both before the stack layers. A failed static layer still fails the run, and `layers.tsv` and the summary still list every layer with its own result and duration. Output from layers running concurrently goes to per-layer logs, so it doesn't interleave; the failed layer's log is printed.

That should save 8 to 10 minutes per full gate.

## Done when
- A full gate runs the static layers while the stack starts, and is that much shorter.
- A failure in any static layer still fails the run and names the layer; rerunning from a failed layer (`./run-tests.sh <layer>...`) works as before.

issues.title: Keep only organization-wide tests in the serial instance phase
issues.body:
The browser suite's instance phase runs one test at a time: 256 tests in 646 s in the last gate, which is 11 of the gate's 43 minutes. The parallel phase ran 499 tests in 368 s.

`e2e/fixtures/projects.ts` puts 30+ spec files into `INSTANCE_SPECS`, because they change what belongs to the organization as a whole. Each of them runs from the organization's settings as the bootstrap left them. It's likely that only some tests in those files really change organization-wide state, such as permissions, brand, sign-in provider or connections. Others only read it, or could make what they need in a team space of their own (`fixtures/team.ts`).

**Change:** go through the instance specs and move every test that doesn't change organization-wide state to the parallel phase. Split a file where only some of its tests need the instance. Where a test changes a setting only to read it back, see if a team-scoped setting or a fixture that restores the setting does the job.

## Done when
- The instance phase holds only the tests that change organization-wide state, each with the reason in `projects.ts`.
- The browser suite passes 3 times in a row with `REPEAT=3`, and the instance phase is at least half as long.

issues.title: Run the integration tests in parallel
issues.body:
`test-integration` takes 10.5 minutes locally. The 282 tests are in one package (`backend/test`, 127 files), none of them calls `t.Parallel()`, and they run under `-race`, so they run strictly one after another against the one stack. CI splits them into 3 jobs of about 6 minutes, each with its own stack.

**Change:** let the integration tests run in parallel:
1. **Shared state:** find what the tests share, such as the organization, site settings, the outbox, the clock and the render service. Give each test its own scratch database where it changes shared state, as Cloudster1/Exciter#282 did with `ownOutbox` (a scratch database plus `seed.Ensure`).
2. **Parallel by default:** mark the tests `t.Parallel()`, and keep the few that must be alone, such as migrations and upgrades, in a serial group with the reason written down.
3. **Cheap first step if (1) is slow to finish:** run the 3 CI shards locally at once, each against its own database on the one stack.

That should bring the layer to about 3 to 4 minutes.

## Done when
- `make test-integration` passes 5 times in a row with the tests running in parallel, and takes under 5 minutes on the gate machine.
- The serial tests are listed, each with its reason.

issues.title: Measure and raise the browser suite's default workers
issues.body:
The browser suite's parallel phase runs with `WORKERS ?= 4` (`mk/e2e.mk`). In the last gate it ran 1368 test-seconds in 368 s. With 6 to 8 workers it should be closer to 3 minutes, if the gate machine has the memory.

`mk/e2e.mk` already says when the kernel killed browsers for lack of memory, so the limit is visible.

**Change:** measure the parallel phase with 4, 6 and 8 workers on the gate machine, with nothing else running and with a second gate running. Then set the default to the best value that never ran out of memory. Alternatively, derive the default from the machine's free memory and cores, capped, so a smaller machine keeps 4.

## Done when
- The default `WORKERS` is the measured best, with the numbers written in the issue.
- The parallel phase passes 3 times in a row at that setting, with no out-of-memory warning.

issues.title: Open the release pull request when the notes are over GitHub's body limit
issues.body:
`./release.sh` for v0.1.0 pushed `release/v0.1.0` but couldn't open its pull request:

```
pull request create failed: GraphQL: Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters) (createPullRequest)
```

The notes of a first release are the whole `Unreleased` section, about 106 KB here, and `release.sh` puts all of them into the pull request body. It opened #491 by hand with a short body instead.

**Fix:** when the body would be over 65,536 characters, write the intro plus a pointer to the release's section of `CHANGELOG.md` in the branch, and cut the notes at a line with a note saying how much is left out. GitHub releases allow 125,000 characters, so the release itself (`--notes-file`) takes the full notes for now. `tests/test-release.sh` should have a case with notes over the limit, checking the stand-in `gh` gets a body under it. Exciter's `release.sh` builds the body the same way.

## Done when
- `release.sh` opens the pull request for notes of any length, and the test covers it.

issues.title: Sign in silently when the identity provider already has a session
issues.body:
Someone signed in to Armature, Stator or Exciter through the suite's Keycloak realm, who then opens another of the three, lands on its sign-in page and has to click "Sign in". Keycloak still has their session, so the click sends them there and straight back, signed in, without a password. The click is all that's left, but it happens on every first visit and on every link from one tool to another. This was seen on a real Dynamo install, where Keycloak returns at once.

**Change:** on a visit without a session, Stator first tries a silent sign-in:
- **The request:** a top-level redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with `prompt=none`, the usual `state`, PKCE and `nonce`, and the page the person asked for.
- **Keycloak still has a session:** the callback signs the person in, as a normal sign-in does, with the same group mapping and membership checks, and returns them to that page.
- **No session** (`error=login_required`, `interaction_required` or `consent_required`): the callback shows the sign-in page as today, and remembers for the browser session (a short-lived cookie) that the silent try already failed, so there's no redirect loop and no second round trip on the next page.
- **Only when single sign-on is configured:** with local accounts only, nothing changes.
- **Not after signing out:** a sign-out sets the same marker, so the person isn't signed straight back in. With RP-initiated logout at the provider, the provider's session ends too.
- **Can be turned off:** a setting, for example `auth.silentSignIn` in the chart, on by default when an OIDC provider is set.

## Done when
- In the integration or browser tests, with a provider that has a session, opening a deep link without a session lands on that page signed in, with no click. Without a provider session, it lands on the sign-in page, and the next page doesn't redirect again.
- After signing out, the next visit shows the sign-in page.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `auth.silent-sign-in@1`, so the suite's tests can rely on it (praetorianer777/Dynamo#2).

issues.title: Link the connected tools in the avatar menu
issues.body:
Clicking one's profile picture opens a small menu. When Stator is connected to Armature or Exciter, that menu should also link to them, so people can switch tools in one click.

## What the menu shows
- Under the account entries, a group "Switch to" with one entry per tool Stator is connected to: its name and its icon.
- Each entry opens that tool's home at the public address of the connection an administrator set up, the one dynamo-connect configures.
- It is a plain link, so the browser's open-in-new-tab works too.
- A tool is listed once the organization's connection to it is configured, whether or not the person connected their own account there; with single sign-on the other tool signs them in.
- A tool that is not connected, or whose connection an administrator removed, is not listed. With none, the group is not shown.
- Everyone signed in sees it, guests included, since the other tool decides what they may see.

## Fits the shared layout
The menus of the three tools are moving to one layout (praetorianer777/Dynamo#12). The group belongs in the avatar menu wherever that layout keeps it, in the same place and under the same name in all three. The same issue is filed in each tool.

## Done when
- With Armature and Exciter connected, the avatar menu lists both and each link opens that tool's home.
- With one connected, only it is listed; with none, the group is gone.
- A test covers each of these.

issues.body:
Stator learns a sign-in provider's group only when one of its members signs in (groups are synced at sign-in, `GET /groups` only). So an administrator, or Dynamo's connect job, cannot grant a realm group access to a space (`PUT /spaces/{key}/permissions`) before anyone in that group has signed in.

Armature already allows it: `POST /groups` with `name` and `externalRef`, matched to the claim at sign-in.

## Done when

- A second request for the same `externalRef` answers 409, or returns the group, as Armature does.
- The group can be named in space permissions straight away.
- Integration test: make the group, grant it on a space, sign in a person of that group, and they see the space.

Needed so the three tools can grant the same access per group (praetorianer777/Dynamo, issue filed with this one).

issues.title: Map a provider group to a read-only standing

A group mapping (`POST /oidc-provider/group-roles`) grants only `member` or `admin` (`grouproles.go`). A realm group of readers therefore gets every grant `everyone` has, such as editing each new space, with no way to admit them read-only by group.

- Integration test: a person in a group mapped this way can sign in and read a space open to everyone, and cannot change it.

Asked for so the three tools give a realm group of readers the same standing everywhere (see the Dynamo issue filed with this one).

issues.title: Mark what a connected app wrote
issues.body:
### User story

As a person reading a page's history, I want to see when a change was made through a connected app rather than by the person themselves, so that I know which writes an assistant or a tool such as Rotor made on someone's behalf.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] What is written through a personal token or a connected app's grant (#449, #469) carries `via`: page versions, comments, remote links, attachments, reactions and the audit log
- [ ] The database writes it: a trigger stamps `via_kind` (`token` or `oauth`), `via_id` and `via_name` from the token or grant the acting person uses, named in a transaction setting beside the acting person; a value sent by hand is overwritten, and changing one is refused
- [ ] Revoking a token or ending a grant keeps its name on what it wrote
- [ ] The API answers `via: {kind, name}` on those resources, null for a session; the webhooks Stator sends carry it on the actor
- [ ] The history, comments and the audit log show "through" and the name beside the person, in English and German

### Tests

Integration: a write through a grant and through a personal token carries `via`; a session write carries none; a hand-set value is overwritten and a change refused, also as `stator_app` in SQL. vitest for the "through" tag; Playwright on the page history.

### Implementation

Port Cloudster1/Exciter#190 (commit c0d072d): `internal/via`, a migration adding the columns and the `via_stamped` trigger reading `app.via`, `db.WithVia` set by the middleware from the principal's token, the read models and webhook actor, and a small "through" component in the web. Credit it in NOTICE.

### Depends on

- #449 (the grants whose app it names)

Needed by Cloudster1/Rotor#105, so a person sees what a workflow wrote as them.

issues.title: Let a connected app take a narrower token for one run
issues.body:
### User story

As a connected app such as Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor), I want a short-lived, narrower access token for one workflow run without changing the person's grant, so that a run holds only what it needs and parallel runs do not fight over the grant's refresh token.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/v1/oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693) accepts a `stator_oat_` access token of the calling client's own grant as `subject_token`
- [ ] `scope` may only narrow the grant's (`read` from a grant that writes); `stator_spaces` may narrow its spaces to ones the grant reaches and the person may see
- [ ] `stator_expires_in` asks for 1 to 3600 seconds; the token never outlives its subject
- [ ] Only an access token is issued, never a refresh token; the grant and its other tokens are untouched, and an exchanged token is not itself a subject
- [ ] Revoking the exchanged token (RFC 7009) ends it alone; ending the grant ends every token exchanged from it
- [ ] A partner app's Keycloak exchange (#469) keeps working unchanged; `oauth.token-exchange@1`'s promise covers the new subject

### Tests

Unit: scope, spaces and lifetime checks. Integration: exchange to `read`, an MCP write refused with it while the grant still writes; a wider scope refused; spaces narrowed; lifetime capped; another client's subject and an exchanged subject refused; revoking the grant ends exchanged tokens; `stator_app` cannot read the exchanged tokens in SQL.

### Implementation

Port Armature's `narrow` (`internal/oauth/token.go`, commit 10edbd7) and its `oauth_exchanged_token` table, as Cloudster1/Exciter#235 did for Exciter; authentication reads an exchanged token as its grant narrowed. Credit it in NOTICE.

### Depends on

- #449 (the client's own grants)

Needed by Cloudster1/Rotor#105, which gives each run a token of its own.

issues.title: Markdown import refuses a file with an HTML img on a line of its own
issues.body: `PUT /api/v1/pages/{id}/markdown` refuses a whole file when it holds an HTML image with an absolute address on a line of its own, as many READMEs do for a logo: ```markdown # T Text. ``` Stator 0.1.0 answers 422: ``` The file index.md cannot be a page: this page puts a "text" where it cannot go; move it out. ``` The same `` with a relative `src` (`a.png`) is taken, and so is one inside a line of text (`Text inline.`). Attributes such as `align="right" width="150"` make no difference. Found by Dynamo's sample import of evcc's README (praetorianer777/Dynamo#34), where the gopher logo is `` and the import makes its address absolute. ## Expected - The image becomes an image block, as `![](https://example.com/a.png)` does, or, failing that, is left out with the rest of the file imported. - A refusal names the line that cannot be placed, so a writer can find it in a long file. https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Share a page and its subpages without access to the space
issues.body:
Today a person reaches a page only through its space: page restrictions narrow what the space grants, and "Also allowed to edit" widens editing but never viewing. To let somebody read one page and the pages below it, a space administrator has to give them view on the whole space and then put a view list on every other page, and every page added later is open to them until somebody restricts it too. That is error-prone and leaks by default.

## What is asked
A **share** of a page: people and groups who may view, or view and edit, that page and everything below it, **without any permission in the space**.

## How it works
- **Who shares:** administrators of the space, in the page's lock dialog, under "Shared with", each entry with **View** or **View and edit**. The share covers the page and every page below it, pages added there later included.
- **What a person with only shares sees:**
  - The space appears in their list of spaces, and its tree holds only the shared pages. The pages above a shared page appear as a path of titles without content, so the person knows where they are; they open nothing else.
  - Search, Recently viewed, the home page, watching, notifications, links, backlinks, includes and excerpts show them nothing outside their shares. A link to an unshared page reads as a restricted page, as today.
  - The space's home page stays hidden unless it is shared itself.
- **View and edit** covers what "Also allowed to edit" covers today: drafts, publishing, live saves, files, labels, appearance, owners and verification. It does not cover adding pages below, moving, copying, importing or deleting; those still take Add pages or Delete in the space. Whether a third level "View, edit and add pages below" is wanted is open for discussion here.
- **Restrictions still bind:** a view list or an edit list on a page below the shared one applies to the person as to everybody, so a share never gets past a restriction set deeper down. Space and site administrators are unaffected.
- **Comments** follow view: a person with a share may comment where the space lets its members comment.
- **Guests** may be shared with in their own space only, as edit grants work today. A token limited to spaces reaches a shared page only in a space it names, a read-only token writes nothing, and a public link is not widened by a share.
- **Moves and copies:** a page moved to another space leaves its shares behind; a copy takes none, as with edit grants.

## Who can see it was shared
- The access report (#81) shows the share as the step that lets the person view or edit, naming the shared page.
- The space's permissions page lists every share in the space: page, person or group, level, and who shared it when, so administrators see who reaches what without space access.
- The audit log records each share added, changed and removed.

## Enforced in the database
As with edit grants, the view and edit rules in the database read the shares, not only the service: a share row is written only by an administrator of the space, and reading or writing a page outside one's shares is refused by the database too. The integration tests try it straight through SQL.

## Done when
- A person with no permission in a space, shared View on a page, reads that page and the pages below it, sees the path above it as titles only, and finds nothing else of the space anywhere: tree, search, recent, links, includes, notifications.
- With View and edit they edit and publish those pages and cannot add, move or delete pages.
- A view list below the shared page keeps them out of that page and the pages below it.
- Removing the share takes it all away at once, open sessions included.
- Only space administrators change shares; the database refuses anybody else.
- Tests at every layer: Go unit, integration (including the database refusing directly), vitest for the dialog and the permissions page, and a Playwright scenario for a shared reader and a shared editor.

issues.title: Test pages, drafts, history, Markdown and live editing end to end
issues.body:
The backend for pages, drafts, history and Markdown is tested closely: versions_test, collab_test, live_pages_test, scheduled_publishing_test and markdown_test assert the effect of every drafts, history and markdown operation, the 404 for a stranger, the 409 codes (publish_conflict, no_draft, conflict, drafts_pending, page_live, page_not_live, room_gone) and the walls on page_version, page_draft, the shared draft and schedules through SQL. Vitest covers the editor's save states, conflicts, history, compare and restore. What is missing: a view-only member is never refused restore, publish or discard; history, publish, replace and mode are never tried on an archived page; `POST /pages` has no title validation test; and several controls on the editor and history routes are never reached by Playwright. In the integration run on main, `DELETE /pages/{pageID}/draft` and `DELETE /pages/{pageID}/schedule` were only ever refused with 401 and 404.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `POST /pages/{pageID}/versions/{versionNumber}/restore` by a member who may only view the space: 403, and `GET /versions` still shows the same total. Today the only restore refusals are the stranger's 404 and the 409s.
- [ ] `POST /pages/{pageID}/publish` by a member who may only view: 403, never no_draft.
- [ ] `DELETE /pages/{pageID}/draft` and `DELETE /pages/{pageID}/schedule` by a member who may only view: 403, and the draft and the schedule are still there.
- [ ] On an archived page, each of these is refused with 409 archived and leaves the page at its version: `POST .../versions/1/restore`, `POST .../publish` of a draft saved before archiving, `PUT .../markdown`, `PUT .../mode`, `PUT .../schedule`, `PUT .../live`. archive_test.go lists PATCH, draft, move, delete and others, but none of these.
- [ ] `PUT /pages/{pageID}/markdown` on a page held to a review rule: 409 review_required, with no new version. On a folder: 409 folder.
- [ ] `POST /pages` with a blank title, a 256 character title, or no parentId: 422 naming the field. `PATCH /pages/{pageID}` with a 256 character title: 422.

Go unit:
- [ ] `internal/markdown/export.go`: withoutEmphasis and sameMark are at 0%, splitEdges at 75%. Test bold text with spaces at both ends (expect ` **bold** `) and two neighbouring links with different hrefs (they must not merge into one).

Playwright:
- [ ] The conflict notice on `/s/$spaceKey/p/$pageId/$slug/edit`, button "Discard draft" (`data-action="discard-conflict"`): the draft is gone and the editor shows the other person's version. versions.spec.ts reaches only "Keep my draft and publish" and "Compare with version N".
- [ ] "Compare with previous" (`data-action="compare-previous"`) on a version row of `/history` opens that comparison.
- [ ] "Older versions" and "Newer versions" on `/history` for a page with more versions than HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE.
- [ ] A stale address puts itself right: `/s/$spaceKey/p/$pageId/old-slug` after a rename lands on the new slug and keeps the `#hash`, and `/s/$spaceKey/p/<home page id>` lands on `/s/$spaceKey`.
- [ ] A view-only member who opens `/edit` sees "You can read this page but not edit it. ..." and no editor. On an archived page they see "This page is archived, so nobody can edit it. ...".
- [ ] "Discard draft" on a page never published asks "Throw your changes away? The page keeps the content it was made with." and the page stays unpublished with its first content.
- [ ] Two people in one shared draft. Taking edit access away from one shows them "You may no longer edit this page, so your changes are no longer shared. ..." and their next words do not reach the other.
- [ ] "Discard draft" in a shared draft asks "Throw the shared draft away for everybody editing it? ..." and the other person's editor starts again from the published page.
- [ ] When the session ends mid edit (cookies cleared), the shared draft shows "Your session ended, so your changes are no longer shared. ...".
- [ ] The "Text style" menu (`data-editor-action="text-style"`) turns a paragraph into Heading 1, 2, 3 and back to Text. versions.spec.ts only opens it and presses Escape.

Vitest:
- [ ] PageEditor in shared draft mode shows t.collab.refused and t.collab.signedOut, and disables Publish, when the session reports either state. session.test.ts covers only the transport logic, and pages/collab.test.tsx covers neither message.
- [ ] PageHistory paging: "Older versions" moves the offset by HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE and is disabled on the last page. "Newer versions" is disabled at offset 0.

Database guards:
- [ ] `page_title_not_blank` (migration 00020): as stator_app, try `UPDATE page SET title = '  '` and an `INSERT INTO page` with a blank title, and watch both refuse. No test reaches this CHECK.

## Done when
- Every drafts, history and markdown operation has an integration test of the view-only 403 and of the archived 409 where those apply.
- Every control in PageEditor, PageHistory and the collab status is clicked by at least one Playwright spec.
- `page_title_not_blank` is tried through SQL.

issues.title: Test the editor's blocks, toolbar and macros end to end

issues.title: Test the page tree and moves end to end
issues.body:
The tree, trash, archive and folder operations (`GET /spaces/{spaceKey}/pages`, `/outline`, `POST /pages/{pageID}/move`, `/copy`, `DELETE /pages/{pageID}`, the 4 trash and 5 archive operations) have strong integration tests: page_tree_test.go, trash_test.go, archive_test.go and folders_test.go, with SQL tests for loops, cross space parents, trash marks, archived rows and folders. What they lack is the refusals that hinge on the target space or the caller's rights, and one SECURITY DEFINER function: in the integration run on main, `POST /spaces/{spaceKey}/trash/{pageID}/restore` was only ever refused with 401 and 404. On the web side, the four specs (page-tree, folders, trash, archive) cover dragging onto a row's middle, the keyboard move dialog, restoring, purging and archiving. "Copy page" (`confirm-copy`) and "Empty trash" (`empty-trash`) are reached by no spec, and neither are moving to another space, moving without children, or reordering by drag. `PlaceDialog` in copy mode has no vitest.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `POST /pages/{pageID}/move` by a member who may arrange pages in the source space but only views the target space: 403 forbidden from the target's `ArrangePages` check (`parentFor`), and the page stays where it was. edit_grants_test only covers a caller who fails the source check first.
- [ ] `GET /spaces/{spaceKey}/trash` and `POST /spaces/{spaceKey}/trash/{pageID}/restore` by a reader of the space (view only, no delete): 403 forbidden. Also restoring a trashed page whose edit list leaves the caller off (they view it but may not delete it, page/trash.go:139): 403, and the page stays in the trash.
- [ ] Restoring a page whose former parent was archived after the deletion: it comes back under the home page, not under the archived page (the `archived_at IS NULL` check in `Restore`), and the trash item said `parentInTree: false`.
- [ ] `POST /pages/{pageID}/copy` with `withChildren: true` by somebody a child's view list leaves out: the hidden child and what is below it are not copied (the `ViewablePage` filter in `Copy`). Assert the copy's children over the API and the row count through SQL.

Playwright:

Word import has only the died part way case. Imports onto an archived page are not tested. - [ ] Space import whose earlier worker died after making the space (`space_import` running, `space_id` set, `lease_until` past): the next claim discards that space and tombstones its files before importing again (the `leftover` path of `runImport`). The job ends done with one space under the key.

issues.body:

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] Retry exhaustion: after the sixth failed attempt (`MaxAttempts`) no seventh row is queued, and the last row is failed with `next_attempt_at` NULL.
- [ ] A retry still pending when a person turns the endpoint off (`PATCH /webhooks/{webhookID}` with `enabled: false`) comes due as cancelled, with the "turned off before this was sent" sentence, and the receiver gets nothing.
- [ ] Topic filter: an endpoint subscribed only to page.published gets no delivery row for page.moved, page.deleted, comment.created or page.remote_link.removed.

- [ ] `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/deliveries/{deliveryID}/redeliver` naming a delivery of another webhook answers 404 and posts nothing.
- [ ] `GET /webhooks/{webhookID}/deliveries`: without limit it answers the 50 newest first, and `limit=500` answers at most `MaxDeliveries` (200).
- [ ] `Prune`: attempts older than `DeliveryRetention` (30 days) are deleted, and pending attempts of any age are kept.
- [ ] Two senders running `SendDue` over the same due deliveries post each one exactly once (the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` lease).

issues.title: Test notifications, watching and mail end to end
issues.body:
The integration suite covers watching and notifications well: `watching_test.go` (every watch kind, moves, trash, opt out), `notifications_test.go` (published and created rows, mark read, preferences, mail sent at once, the daily digest, two workers) and `watch_notify_rls_test.go` (the RLS walls through SQL). - [ ] Hourly digest: with `digest: "hourly"`, `notify.NewDigester(...).WithClock(...).Once` sends nothing before the next full hour after the oldest queued row. At that hour it sends one bundle to Mailpit whose subject counts every unread row, then empties `notification_digest`.

issues.title: Keep every automatic webhook retry after a manual redelivery
issues.body:
## Problem

Redelivering a webhook delivery by hand while the event's next automatic retry is still pending cuts the event's retries short. `Redeliver` in `backend/internal/webhook/deliver.go` gives the manual delivery the next attempt number (`max(attempt) + 1`), which is the number the automatic chain needs for its following retry. When the pending retry fails, `record` inserts that retry with `ON CONFLICT (endpoint_id, event_id, attempt) DO NOTHING`, the insert is dropped, and the event is given up after two of its `MaxAttempts` automatic attempts.

## Done when

- A manual redelivery no longer takes an attempt number the automatic retries need, so the event keeps all of its automatic attempts.
- An integration test redelivers while a retry is pending, lets the endpoint keep failing, and counts every automatic attempt.

- **Editor preview:** `POST /api/v1/diagrams`, with a language and text, answers the SVG. It is for people who may edit, and is rate-limited per person.
- **Readers:** a per-page endpoint by hash serves the page's diagrams, checked against the page, so guests and public pages work.

- **Errors** are sentences: Kroki's first error line for a diagram it can't read, "took too long to draw" for a timeout or a bare 500, and "cannot be drawn right now" when Kroki is down.

- **PDF export** prints the drawing when there is one, and the source with that sentence when there isn't.

issues.title: Grant access through roles, a permission matrix, groups and grants
issues.body:
The three tools grant access one way, set out in [docs/administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#access) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75): roles, a permission matrix, groups and grants, as Armature has them (Cloudster1/Armature `backend/migrations/00010_rbac.sql`, `web/src/features/access/RoleMatrix.tsx`, `RoleTable.tsx`, `GroupList.tsx`, the `/roles`, `/permissions`, `/groups` and `/role-assignments` endpoints).

Stator has fixed organization roles today (owner, admin, member, guest). It grants rights directly in grids of who against what: one for the whole organization (use, create spaces, administer), and one per space (view, add pages, add comments, delete, administer). Group roles map a provider group straight to Member or Admin. There are no roles one can define, and changing what a level means means editing every space's grid.

## Done when
- **Roles** are data: built-in ones that cannot be deleted, and ones administrators add, rename and delete.
  - The built-in roles are an administrator over the whole installation, and in a space viewer, commenter, editor and space administrator.
  - Each lists its permissions outright, with no inheritance.
- **The Matrix tab** lists every permission Stator checks against every role. A box saves when ticked; the administrator's right to administer stays ticked.
- **Groups** are added by hand or carry a provider claim. Provider memberships are replaced at every sign-in. A built-in Everyone group holds every member.
- **Grants** are a role, a scope (the whole installation or one space) and a subject (a person or a group). What somebody may do in a space is the union of the grants that reach them. A space's permissions page grants roles instead of ticking rights.
- **Restrictions** on single pages keep narrowing what a grant allows, as today.
- **Buttons** are decided by permission, never by a role's name.
- **Migration:** every grid entry and group role of today moves to the grant of the built-in role it amounts to, so nobody's access changes. The upgrade test proves that for a seeded installation.
- **Single sign-on:** "Let people in by their groups" (#583) admits by a group that holds a grant.
- **The database** keeps the guards it has: row level security reads the grants, and the installation keeps an active administrator.
- **Tests:**
  - grants through a person, a group, Everyone and the whole installation;
  - a renamed role and a new role reaching buttons and the API;
  - a provider group removed at sign-in taking its grants along;
  - the migration.

Related: the Admin layout is its own issue, and the Access tabs live there.

issues.title: Give every page a confidentiality level
issues.body:
### User story

As an editor, I want to mark a page public, internal, confidential or secret, so that apps reading the wiki for someone, such as Rotor's workflow runs, can be kept away from sensitive pages.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Four fixed levels, ordered `public < internal < confidential < secret`; a page stores its own level, `internal` by default (existing pages included)
- [ ] A page's effective level is the highest of its own and its ancestors', as view restrictions inherit; moving a page recomputes it for the page and everything below
- [ ] Anyone who may edit the page may raise its level; only a space administrator may lower it, and the database refuses anything else for `stator_app`
- [ ] `PUT /api/v1/pages/{id}/confidentiality` sets it; `Page` (and so `get_page`) returns `confidentiality` with `level`, `effective`, `inheritedFrom` and `canLower`
- [ ] Setting a level is not an edit: no new version, no published stamp, no change to `updated_*`
- [ ] Each change writes the audit event `page.confidentiality_set` with the old and new level
- [ ] Webhook page payloads carry the effective level
- [ ] Levels do not change what a person sees; they only cap tokens (#597)

### Tests

Unit: level ordering and the raise and lower rule. Integration: an editor raises a level; an editor lowering one is refused by the API and again straight through SQL as `stator_app`; a space administrator lowers it; a child under a confidential page reads as confidential and stops once moved out; the audit row and the webhook payload carry the level; a change creates no version.

### Implementation

- A satellite table `page_confidentiality`, kept out of the `page` row as `page_owner` is (migration 00250), so `page_write_guard` does not read a change as an edit
- `page_effective_confidentiality(page)` in SQL, walking ancestors as view-restriction inheritance does (00090)
- A new action in `internal/perm` for lowering a level, held by space administrators

### Depends on

Nothing.

Needed by Cloudster1/Rotor#164, through #597.

- [ ] The page header shows a badge with the effective level

- [ ] Levels below the current one are disabled unless the person may lower it, and the dialog says who may
- [ ] An inherited level says from which page it comes, with a link
- [ ] Strings live in `web/src/i18n/en.ts` and `de.ts`; the audit log labels `page.confidentiality_set`
- [ ] axe passes in light and dark

### Tests

### Implementation

issues.title: Cap an app's token at a confidentiality level
issues.body:
### User story

As a connected app such as Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor), I want a token that cannot read pages above a confidentiality level I name, so that a workflow run never sees what its workflow is not cleared for, even with the person's full permissions behind it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Token exchange (#499) accepts `stator_max_confidentiality=<level>`; it only narrows, so an exchanged token never has a higher cap than its subject, and a wider one is refused
- [ ] Personal access tokens may carry a cap, set when the token is made
- [ ] The cap is enforced in the database on every path that reads a page's content or title:
  - `perm_page_viewable`
  - `page_search_rows`, `attachment_search_hits` and `comment_search_hits`, including the `perm_space_plain` fast path
  - outlines and listings: `page_outline_rows`, pages below, recent and updated pages, label pages, `properties_report`
  - versions, comments, attachments, excerpts and includes of a capped page
  - markdown, PDF and Word renderings
- [ ] A capped page answers "not found", as a page the person cannot see does, never a refusal that names it
- [ ] `/meta` advertises `confidentiality@1` and lists the levels in order
- [ ] `docs/integration.md` documents the parameter; `docs/mcp.md` notes the cap

### Tests

Integration: a token capped at `internal` reads an internal page and gets "not found" from `get_page`, `search`, the space outline, versions, comments and markdown for a confidential page and for its child. Exchange: a narrower cap is accepted, a wider one refused, a capped subject cannot be widened. Every reading MCP tool runs with a capped token. The same reads straight through SQL as `stator_app` with the cap set return nothing.

### Implementation

- `api_token.max_confidentiality`, and the same on the exchanged-token table from #499
- A per-transaction setting `app.token_max_confidentiality`, set in `authenticate` (`httpapi/middleware.go`) as `app.token_spaces` is
- A check beside `perm_token_reaches` (00310) that applies only when the actor is the caller, as the token's spaces do, so workers asking about other people are unaffected

### Depends on

- #595

Needed by Cloudster1/Rotor#164, which caps each run's token at its workflow's level.

issues.title: Find pages when a word is mistyped
issues.body:
Stator's search is full text only (`websearch_to_tsquery` over `search_vector`, migration 00100; the palette's quick search is a prefix `to_tsquery`). A word typed with one letter wrong, "kubernets" or "Konfiguraton", finds nothing, and the search page says there is nothing to find. Exciter already uses `pg_trgm` (its migration 01040).

## Proposal

Correct the words, not the matching: search keeps its full text and its rights checks, and a word that matches nothing is replaced by the closest word Stator holds.

- **Vocabulary**: a table of the lexemes of the organization's pages, comments and file names, taken from their `search_vector`, with a trigram index (`pg_trgm`, `gin_trgm_ops`) and the tenant policy every table has. Writes add their lexemes; the migration fills it from what is there. A word left behind by a deleted page does no harm, since it is only offered when it finds something the reader may see.
- **Full search**: when the query finds nothing, each word whose lexeme is not in the vocabulary is replaced by the most similar one above a threshold, and the search runs again through `page_search_rows` and the attachment and comment hit functions, as now. The answer says which query it ran.
- **Search page**: "Showing results for **kubernetes**. Search instead for kubernets", the second a link that searches exactly as typed (a parameter that turns correction off). In German too.
- **Quick search and the palette**: when the prefix finds fewer pages than asked for, the corrected words fill the rest, without a notice.
- **Nothing leaks**: a correction is only shown when the corrected search finds hits the reader may view, so a word from a page they cannot see is never offered.

## Done when

- A page titled or containing "Kubernetes" is found by "kubernets", "Kuberntes" and "kubernetes" in the full search, the quick search and the palette, and an exact match still ranks first.
- The search page shows the correction and the link to search as typed; the API's answer names the corrected query, documented in the OpenAPI.
- A word only in a page the reader may not view is never offered as a correction (integration test with two readers).
- A query with no near word still says nothing was found.
- Search over the seeded data is no slower when the query matches as typed; the correction adds at most one indexed vocabulary lookup per unknown word.
- Tests: unit tests for the correction, integration tests for the three searches and the rights, vitest for the notice and the link, a browser test that searches with a typo and follows "Search instead for".

issues.title: Report mcp@1 now that partners reach POST /mcp over OAuth
issues.body:
## User story

As a person in the suite, I want Rotor's workflows to read and write Stator pages as me, so that Stator joins workflows the way Armature and Exciter already do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/v1/meta` reports `mcp@1`, with the promise Dynamo's `docs/compatibility.md` gives it once praetorianer777/Dynamo#92 lands: the tool serves its own operations as MCP tools at `POST /mcp`, behind its OAuth
- [ ] `capabilities.go` names `POST /mcp` and the protected-resource metadata as the operations of `mcp@1`, and the capability test lists it

## Tests

The capability unit test in `backend/internal/httpapi/capabilities_test.go`.

## Implementation

Since #449, partners reach `POST /mcp` over OAuth and Stator reports `oauth.partner-tokens@1`, but not `mcp@1`. Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor) offers a tool to its workflows only when the tool reports `mcp@1` (`backend/internal/tools/needs.go` there), as Armature and Exciter do, so Stator cannot be connected yet (Cloudster1/Rotor#105).

## Depends on

- praetorianer777/Dynamo#92 (the promise of `mcp@1`)

issues.title: Let an administrator allow a pending app over the API
issues.body:
## User story

As the suite's operator, I want dynamo-connect to allow Rotor's partner app at Stator over the API, so that a fresh suite has Rotor's workflows reading and writing Stator pages without an administrator clicking through a consent page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An administrator allows a pending app with `POST /api/v1/oauth/clients/{id}/approve` (or the same as a `PATCH` of its status), and its status becomes `allowed` for everybody, as the consent flow's `allowApp` does today
- [ ] Allowing an app that is already allowed changes nothing and answers success, so a rerun of dynamo-connect is a no-op
- [ ] Allowing an unknown or deleted app answers 404 with a sentence; a member who is not an administrator is refused
- [ ] No authorization code is issued, unlike allowing through `POST /oauth/consent`
- [ ] The change is audited with the administrator as the actor, and the OpenAPI document lists the route

## Tests

Integration: an app registered at `POST /oauth/register` is pending, an administrator allows it through the route, and a person's code flow then succeeds without the administrator's consent step; a reader is refused; a second call changes nothing.

## Implementation

Today a pending RFC 7591 app is allowed only through `POST /api/v1/oauth/consent` with `{"query": "<authorize query>", "decision": "allow"}` from an administrator's session (`oauth_consent_handlers.go`, `oauth.Service.Decide` calling `allowApp` in `oauth/authorize.go`). That needs a whole authorize query and leaves an unredeemed code behind. `GET /oauth/clients` already lists pending apps; the route beside it reuses `allowApp`. Armature has the same route (`POST /oauth/clients/{id}/approve`), which dynamo-connect already calls.

Dynamo wires Rotor in praetorianer777/Dynamo#97; Rotor adds Stator in Cloudster1/Rotor#105.

## Depends on

Nothing.
